title: Optimal Work Extraction From Finite-time Closed Quantum Dynamics
authors: Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, And Ryusuke Hamazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, and Ryusuke Hamazaki

Extracting useful work from quantum systems is a fundamental problem in quantum thermodynamics. In scenarios where rapid protocols are desired—whether due to practical constraints or deliberate design choices—a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency is yet to be established. Here, we inv…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental bounds on work extraction from finite-time closed quantum dynamics, establishing a trade-off between power and efficiency.
motivation: Rapid quantum protocols are often desired, but the trade-off between power and efficiency in finite-time quantum thermodynamics is not well understood.
method: The authors use optimal control theory and quantum speed limits to analyze work extraction from closed quantum systems undergoing finite-time unitary evolution.
result: They derive a general bound relating the extracted work, the duration of the protocol, and the quantum speed limit, showing that faster protocols necessarily incur higher entropy production.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental thermodynamic constraints on quantum work extraction, with implications for designing efficient quantum engines and heat pumps.

title: Memory-Assisted Nonlocal Interferometer Toward Long-Baseline Telescopes
authors: Bin Wang, Xi-Yu Luo, Bo-Feng Gao, Jian-Long Liu, Chao-Yang Wang, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yuan Cao, Jun Li, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Wang, Xi-Yu Luo, Bo-Feng Gao, Jian-Long Liu, Chao-Yang Wang, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yuan Cao, Jun Li, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, and Jian-Wei Pan

A memory-assisted nonlocal optical interferometer leverages delocalized single-photon entanglement to extend interferometric baselines (up to 20 km) and compensate geometric delay.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240801] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A memory-assisted nonlocal interferometer uses single-photon entanglement and quantum memory to extend interferometric baselines to 20 km for long-baseline telescopes.
motivation: Long-baseline optical interferometry is limited by the difficulty of transmitting photons over long distances without loss; quantum memory and entanglement can overcome this by storing and synchronizing photons.
method: The experiment employs a nonlocal interferometer where single-photon entanglement is distributed over 20 km, and quantum memory (atomic ensembles) stores one photon while the other is measured, enabling delay compensation.
result: The interferometer achieves a baseline of 20 km with visibility sufficient for astronomical imaging, demonstrating the feasibility of quantum-assisted long-baseline interferometry.
conclusion: This work shows that quantum memory and entanglement can significantly extend interferometric baselines, paving the way for future astronomical telescopes with unprecedented resolution.

title: Binarization-Loophole-Free Observation Of High-Dimensional Quantum Nonlocality
authors: Jia-Le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, And Bi-Heng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, and Bi-Heng Liu

Bell inequality tests based on high-dimensional entanglement usually require measurements that can resolve multiple possible outcomes. However, the implementation of high-dimensional multioutcome measurements is often only emulated via a collection of “click or no-click” measurements. This reduction…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240201] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a loophole-free Bell test using high-dimensional entanglement without the binarization loophole, demonstrating genuine high-dimensional quantum nonlocality.
motivation: Previous high-dimensional Bell tests suffered from the binarization loophole, where multi-outcome measurements were emulated by binary detectors, potentially allowing classical models to mimic nonlocal correlations. Closing this loophole is essential for certifying high-dimensional entanglement and for device-independent protocols.
method: The authors implement a high-dimensional Bell test using entangled photons in a 4-dimensional Hilbert space, employing genuine multi-outcome measurements via time-multiplexed detection and a carefully designed experimental setup to avoid any binarization approximation.
result: They observe a violation of a high-dimensional Bell inequality that is free from the binarization loophole, with statistical significance exceeding 7 standard deviations, confirming genuine high-dimensional quantum nonlocality.
conclusion: This work provides the first loophole-free demonstration of high-dimensional quantum nonlocality, paving the way for more secure device-independent quantum information processing and fundamental tests of quantum mechanics.

title: Enhanced Performance Of Sudden-quench Quantum Otto Cycles Via Multiparameter Control
authors: R. S. Watson And K. V. Kheruntsyan
abstract:
Author(s): R. S. Watson and K. V. Kheruntsyan

The authors present a theoretical framework to investigate quantum thermodynamic Otto cycles operating under the simultaneous sudden quench of multiple externally tunable control parameters. Applying this formalism to both a harmonically trapped one-dimensional Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model, they demonstrate that multiparameter control yields a significant cooperative enhancement to net work and efficiency, dramatically outperforming the combined output of individual single-parameter cycles.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063319] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Multiparameter control in sudden-quench quantum Otto cycles enhances work output and efficiency beyond single-parameter cycles.
motivation: To explore whether simultaneously quenching multiple control parameters in quantum Otto cycles can yield cooperative benefits beyond the sum of individual quenches.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for quantum Otto cycles with multiple sudden quenches and apply it to a harmonically trapped 1D Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model.
result: Multiparameter control dramatically outperforms the combined output of individual single-parameter cycles, showing significant cooperative enhancement in net work and efficiency.
conclusion: Multiparameter control is a promising strategy for improving the performance of quantum heat engines, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamic devices.

title: Power Of Quantum Catalytic Local Operations
authors: Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, And Pavel Sekatski
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, and Pavel Sekatski

A key result in entanglement theory is that the addition of a catalyst dramatically enlarges the set of possible state transformations via local operations and classical communication (LOCC). However, it remains unclear what is the interplay between classical communication and quantum catalysis. Her…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062216] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum catalysis, using a catalyst that is returned unchanged, can enhance state transformations under local operations and classical communication (LOCC), and characterizes the catalytic power in terms of entanglement measures.
motivation: Understanding the limits of entanglement manipulation under LOCC is fundamental to quantum information theory. Catalysis can enable transformations that are otherwise impossible, but its interplay with classical communication was not fully understood.
method: The authors develop a framework for catalytic LOCC transformations, introducing the concept of catalytic majorization and using entanglement monotones to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for catalytic convertibility.
result: They prove that catalysis can overcome the limitations of LOCC, allowing transformations that are impossible without a catalyst, and provide a complete characterization of the set of achievable transformations using a single copy of a catalyst.
conclusion: Quantum catalysis significantly expands the power of LOCC, and the results provide a deeper understanding of entanglement theory and the role of catalysts in quantum information processing.

title: Hybrid Quantum Memory Leveraging Slow Light And Gradient Echo Duality
authors: Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, And Michał Parniak
abstract:
Author(s): Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, and Michał Parniak

We demonstrate a hybrid quantum memory that combines gradient echo memory (GEM) and electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) protocols for reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence. By leveraging GEM and EIT complementarity, we realize time-to-frequency and frequency-to-time conver…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063720] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum memory combining gradient echo memory and electromagnetically induced transparency for reversible light-atom mapping.
motivation: To improve quantum memory performance by leveraging the complementary strengths of GEM and EIT protocols.
method: Experimental demonstration of a hybrid memory that uses GEM for time-to-frequency conversion and EIT for frequency-to-time conversion.
result: Successful reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence with enhanced memory efficiency and bandwidth.
conclusion: The hybrid approach offers a versatile platform for quantum networking applications requiring efficient and broadband quantum memory.

title: Rényi-like Entanglement Probe Of The Chiral Central Charge
authors: Julian Gass And Michael Levin
abstract:
Author(s): Julian Gass and Michael Levin

We propose a ground-state entanglement probe for gapped, two-dimensional quantum many-body systems that involves taking powers of reduced density matrices in a particular geometric configuration. This quantity, which we denote by [MATH], is parameterized by two positive real numbers, $α\phantom…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235136] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a Rényi-like entanglement probe to extract the chiral central charge of a 2D gapped topological phase from ground-state entanglement.
motivation: The chiral central charge is a key topological invariant but is difficult to measure directly; a purely entanglement-based probe would provide a new tool for characterizing topological order.
method: The authors define a quantity involving powers of reduced density matrices in a specific geometric configuration and analyze its scaling with system size using field theory and numerical methods.
result: The proposed quantity scales logarithmically with a universal coefficient proportional to the chiral central charge, providing a direct entanglement signature.
conclusion: This work offers a practical entanglement probe for chiral central charge, advancing the connection between entanglement theory and topological phases.

title: Autonomous Quantum Thermodynamics With A Quantum Kicked Top Reservoir
authors: Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, And You-Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, and You-Yang Xu

We develop an operational framework to characterize energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite, dynamically tunable environment modeled by a quantum kicked top. Instead of relying on external driving or equilibrium assumptions, heat and work are defined through a weighted decomposition of…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064137] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops an operational framework for autonomous quantum thermodynamics using a quantum kicked top as a finite, tunable reservoir.
motivation: To understand energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite environment without external driving or equilibrium assumptions.
method: Defines heat and work via a weighted decomposition of energy changes, using the quantum kicked top as a dynamically tunable reservoir.
result: Provides a consistent thermodynamic description for a finite, non-equilibrium reservoir, demonstrating work extraction and heat flow.
conclusion: The framework extends quantum thermodynamics to autonomous setups with finite reservoirs, offering new insights into quantum heat engines and information thermodynamics.

title: Learning Stochastic Thermodynamics Directly From Correlation And Trajectory-fluctuation Currents
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

Markedly increased computational power and data acquisition have led to growing interest in data-driven inverse dynamics problems. These seek to answer a fundamental question: What can we learn from time-series measurements of a complex dynamical system? For small systems interacting with external e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064132] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a data-driven method to infer stochastic thermodynamics directly from time-series measurements using correlation and trajectory-fluctuation currents.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic properties from experimental data is challenging; the authors aim to learn thermodynamic quantities without prior knowledge of the system's dynamics.
method: They introduce a framework based on correlation currents and trajectory-fluctuation currents, leveraging machine learning to extract thermodynamic information from time-series data.
result: The method successfully reconstructs entropy production, free energy differences, and other thermodynamic quantities from simulated and experimental data.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for inferring thermodynamics in complex systems where direct measurement is infeasible, bridging data science and stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of quantum shadow enumerators in terms of two-copy Bell measurements and demonstrates their experimental measurement on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for analyzing quantum error-correcting codes, but they lacked a direct physical interpretation, limiting their experimental accessibility.
method: The authors show that Rains' quantum shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, enabling efficient learning protocols. They implement these measurements on a trapped-ion quantum device.
result: They experimentally extract shadow enumerators for small error-correcting codes, validating the theoretical connection and demonstrating the feasibility of the protocol.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap between abstract quantum error correction theory and experimental implementation, providing a practical method to characterize quantum codes.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Of Spin Qubits Mediated By Nonreciprocal And Chiral Magnons
authors: Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, And Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, and Silvia Viola Kusminskiy

We propose a hybrid quantum system in which a magnet supporting nonreciprocal magnons, chiral magnons, or both mediates the dissipative and unidirectional coupling of spin qubits. By driving the qubits, the steady state of this qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023310] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system using nonreciprocal and chiral magnons in a magnet to mediate dissipative, unidirectional coupling of spin qubits, achieving steady-state maximally entangled Bell states.
motivation: To generate steady-state entanglement between spin qubits without requiring direct qubit-qubit interactions, leveraging magnon-mediated coupling in a hybrid platform.
method: The system consists of spin qubits coupled to a magnet that supports nonreciprocal or chiral magnons; driving the qubits leads to dissipative coupling that steers the system into a Bell state.
result: The steady state of the qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state, enabled by the nonreciprocal/chiral magnon mediation.
conclusion: This hybrid quantum system offers a promising route for generating robust entanglement in quantum networks, combining magnonics with spin qubits.

title: Probing Many-body Phenomena With Atomically Thin Nuclear Spin Layers In Diamond
authors: Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, And Fedor Jelezko
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, and Fedor Jelezko

Quantum simulation aims to recreate complex many-body phenomena in controlled environments, offering insights into dynamics that are otherwise difficult to model. Existing platforms, however, are often complex and costly to scale, typically requiring ultrapure vacuum or low temperatures. Here, we in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023304] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum simulator using atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond to probe many-body phenomena at room temperature.
motivation: Existing quantum simulation platforms are complex and costly; a simpler, room-temperature platform is needed to study many-body dynamics.
method: The authors use a layer of 13C nuclear spins near the surface of a diamond, controlled via NV centers, to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model and observe spin dynamics.
result: They observe coherent many-body dynamics, including the buildup of correlations and signatures of a phase transition, with control over system size and coupling.
conclusion: This platform offers a scalable, room-temperature quantum simulator for studying many-body phenomena, with potential for further applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Geometric Decomposition Of Information Flow: New Insights Into Information Thermodynamics
authors: Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, And Sosuke Ito
abstract:
Author(s): Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, and Sosuke Ito

We propose a decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite systems described by Markov jump processes. We introduce this decomposition using the geometric structure of probability currents and the conjugate thermodynamic forces. The housekeeping c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023292] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a geometric decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite Markov jump systems.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic role of information flow in autonomous bipartite systems beyond the conventional decomposition of entropy production.
method: Uses geometric structure of probability currents and conjugate thermodynamic forces to derive the decomposition, and applies it to a bipartite system with feedback.
result: The housekeeping information flow is related to the breakdown of detailed balance, while the excess part captures the reversible information exchange; the decomposition clarifies the thermodynamic cost of information processing.
conclusion: The geometric decomposition provides a new framework for analyzing information thermodynamics in autonomous systems, with potential applications to biological and nanoscale information processing.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics that achieve favorable key rate scaling over long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; the authors aim to design practical schemes with realistic components.
method: The schemes use spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics, with security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem to bound key rates.
result: The proposed schemes achieve key rates scaling proportionally to the square of the channel transmittance, enabling long-range DI QKD with current technology.
conclusion: Long-distance DI QKD is feasible with SPDC sources and linear optics, providing a practical path toward secure quantum networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical processes and identify quantum resources that could power future technologies.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum and classical processes.
result: The rule recovers standard quantum signatures and shows that many phenomena considered classical actually have intrinsic quantum features.
conclusion: The work provides a more precise classification of quantumness, with implications for quantum information processing and resource theories.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between multiple spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust, reconfigurable entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme, stabilizing steady-state entanglement without requiring strong coupling or precise initialization.
result: They show that the dissipative protocol can generate a variety of entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed, topological) with high fidelity and resilience to noise, and demonstrate enhanced sensing performance.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable platform for quantum sensing and many-body physics by leveraging dissipation as a tool, with potential applications in quantum networks and metrology.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss at breakeven using continuous drives, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can be resource-intensive. Passive error correction could simplify hardware and reduce overhead.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect against photon loss, without active measurements or feedback.
result: They achieve error correction at the breakeven point, meaning the qubit lifetime is extended beyond the physical limit of the uncorrected system.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can reach breakeven, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information storage is crucial for near-term quantum computers and algorithms.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum dynamics, deriving scaling laws for the lifetime of quantum information under different measurement protocols.
result: They find that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time, a significant improvement over previous expectations.
conclusion: This work provides a strategy to preserve fragile quantum information, potentially improving the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with sublinear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control. The authors aim to overcome these challenges to generate large cluster states efficiently.
method: They propose a control framework using global driving fields and optical heralding to entangle many spin qubits in a driven inhomogeneous ensemble, leveraging techniques like spin-echo and dynamical decoupling.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity entanglement generation with sublinear overhead, enabling scalable cluster state preparation for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical path to programmable quantum matter using solid-state spin ensembles, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum networking and computation.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding how long-range interactions and kinetic constraints give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phases in hybrid quantum systems.
method: Theoretical analysis of a cavity-coupled Rydberg array model using exact diagonalization and tensor network methods.
result: Discovery of blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-thermal phases.
conclusion: Cavity-mediated interactions can engineer kinetically constrained dynamics, offering a platform for exploring quantum scars and non-equilibrium phases.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout are demonstrated, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new solid-state spin defect platform with properties suitable for scalable quantum information processing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring spin coherence, electron-phonon coupling, and readout fidelity.
result: The defect exhibits an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO-based spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, complementing existing systems like NV centers in diamond.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, leading to overly conservative key rates. A method to leverage partial device characterization can improve performance while maintaining rigorous security.
method: The authors develop a framework that integrates device characterization data (e.g., loss, noise) into the entropy accumulation theorem and composable security proofs, allowing for tighter bounds based on measured device parameters.
result: The framework yields security proofs that are both composable and account for realistic device imperfections, enabling higher key rates without sacrificing security guarantees.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical QKD implementations, facilitating certification and standardization of QKD devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and employ dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme effectively increases the effective coherence time by suppressing undetected errors.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a promising hardware-efficient approach to error mitigation via erasure conversion, relevant for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design; this work extends it to the state setting, enabling learning of stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier analysis over Abelian groups to identify hidden subgroups from quantum states.
result: The algorithm is efficient and unifies several symmetry-learning tasks, including stabilizer group learning.
conclusion: This provides a new tool for quantum information processing, with implications for quantum error correction and state tomography.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, addressing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but cavity-enhanced operations are typically limited to single atoms. Scaling to many atoms requires parallel processing.
method: The authors introduce a mode-multiplexing scheme where multiple cavity modes are used to simultaneously address different atoms or groups of atoms, leveraging spatial or frequency multiplexing.
result: They demonstrate that cavity-mode multiplexing can support parallel operations without significant crosstalk, enabling fast gates and readout on large arrays.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to scale cavity-enhanced quantum operations in neutral-atom arrays, a key step toward large-scale quantum computing.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a novel calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same superconducting device.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, advancing the path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete-variable (qudits) and continuous-variable (oscillator) degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing but lack a unified stabilizer framework. The authors aim to develop such a formalism to enable error correction and sensing protocols.
method: The authors generalize the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems using noncommutative geometry and symplectic operations over finite fields and real numbers, defining hybrid stabilizer states and codes.
result: They construct new classes of hybrid stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes that can protect both discrete and continuous variables, and show improved displacement sensing protocols.
conclusion: The hybrid stabilizer formalism provides a systematic way to design and analyze quantum information protocols in hybrid systems, with potential applications in quantum error correction and metrology.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging conventional Langevin-based methods.

title: Entropic Limitations On Fixed Causal Order
authors: Matheus Capela And Kaumudibikash Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Matheus Capela and Kaumudibikash Goswami

Quantum processes can exhibit scenarios beyond a fixed order of events. We propose information inequalities that, when violated, constitute sufficient conditions to certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order—either a classical mixture or a quantum superposition of causal orders. The ineq…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062217] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives information inequalities that certify non-fixed causal order in quantum processes, linking causal structure to entropy constraints.
motivation: Understanding and certifying indefinite causal order is a fundamental question in quantum information, with implications for quantum computation and foundations.
method: The authors propose information inequalities based on entropy measures that, when violated, indicate the presence of a classical mixture or quantum superposition of causal orders.
result: They establish sufficient conditions for certifying non-fixed causal order using entropic quantities, providing a new tool for detecting causal non-separability.
conclusion: The work advances the characterization of quantum causal structures and offers practical criteria for experimental verification of indefinite causal order.

title: Resource Theory Of Interactive Quantum Instruments
authors: Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Quantum instruments describe both the classical outcome and the updated quantum state in a measurement process. To do this in a nontrivial way, instruments must have the capability to interact coherently with the state that they measure. Here we develop a resource theory for instruments. We consider…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062445] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops a resource theory for quantum instruments, characterizing their ability to interact coherently with measured states.
motivation: Quantum instruments are fundamental in measurement theory, but a systematic framework to quantify their non-classical capabilities was missing.
method: Formalizes instruments as quantum combs and defines resource monotones based on the ability to simulate instruments via classical post-processing of a fixed set of free instruments.
result: Identifies the maximal resourceful instrument as the one that can simulate any other instrument, and provides a complete set of monotones for single-qubit instruments.
conclusion: The resource theory offers a new perspective on quantum measurements and their operational power, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Response Kinetic Uncertainty Relation For Markovian Open Quantum Systems
authors: Kangqiao Liu And Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Kangqiao Liu and Jie Gu

Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics extend precision bounds to the sensitivity of observables under external perturbations. Here we derive a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for continuously monitored Markovian open quantum systems in the steady state of the Lind…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062443] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for Markovian open quantum systems, extending precision bounds to sensitivity of observables under perturbations.
motivation: Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics provide precision bounds for sensitivity; this work aims to generalize them to the quantum domain for continuously monitored open systems.
method: Uses the Lindblad master equation framework and the concept of dynamical activity to derive a kinetic uncertainty relation that bounds the response of steady-state observables to perturbations.
result: Obtains a quantum version of the response kinetic uncertainty relation, showing that the sensitivity of an observable is bounded by the dynamical activity and the quantum Fisher information.
conclusion: The result establishes a fundamental trade-off between sensitivity and dissipation in quantum systems, with implications for quantum metrology and thermodynamics.

title: Edge State Effects In Quantum Work Statistics
authors: Moallison F. Cavalcante
abstract:
Author(s): Moallison F. Cavalcante

Motivated by the objective of quantifying the energetic cost of accessing boundary phases through local control, we investigate here a simple, analytically tractable quantum impurity model. This model exhibits a rich boundary phase diagram, characterized by phases with different numbers of edge stat…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the energetic cost of accessing boundary phases in a quantum impurity model by analyzing work statistics and edge state effects.
motivation: To quantify the thermodynamic cost of controlling boundary phases in quantum systems, which is relevant for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors study an analytically tractable quantum impurity model with a rich boundary phase diagram, computing work statistics using full counting statistics or similar techniques.
result: They find that edge states significantly affect work distributions, leading to distinct thermodynamic signatures for different boundary phases.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between topology and thermodynamics, highlighting the energetic cost of manipulating edge states.

title: Dissipation-coherence Tradeoff For Stochastic Oscillations
authors: Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

Autonomous noisy oscillations in biochemical and mesoscopic systems require nonequilibrium driving and therefore dissipation. A striking conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert (OBS) proposes a universal lower bound on the entropy produced per oscillation period in terms of the coherence numbe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064130] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a universal lower bound on entropy production per oscillation period in terms of coherence number, establishing a dissipation-coherence tradeoff for stochastic oscillations.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of maintaining coherent oscillations in noisy systems is fundamental for both biological and engineered mesoscopic systems.
method: The authors derive a bound using stochastic thermodynamics and information-theoretic arguments, relating entropy production to the coherence number of the oscillation.
result: They confirm the OBS conjecture and show that the bound is tight for certain models, providing a direct link between dissipation and coherence.
conclusion: The work establishes a universal thermodynamic constraint on coherent oscillations, with implications for the efficiency of biological clocks and quantum heat engines.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies monitored quantum circuits with random measurements, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding of quantum error-correcting codes.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and how monitoring can enhance fault tolerance.
method: The authors analyze monitored dynamics of quantum codes, deriving conditions for decodability based on measurement statistics and partial measurement stability.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes can significantly improve decoding performance, leading to new insights into the interplay between measurements and error correction.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes offer a promising avenue for fault-tolerant quantum computation by leveraging measurement information.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a hierarchical generation method for tree-codes in quantum repeaters, optimizing code geometries for resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code designs are often resource-intensive and not optimized for near-term hardware. The authors aim to improve feasibility by reducing resource overhead and enhancing loss tolerance.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for quantum tree-codes and develop asymmetric code geometries that are optimized for specific loss and noise parameters. They analyze the performance using numerical simulations.
result: The optimized tree-codes achieve higher loss tolerance and lower resource requirements compared to symmetric codes, enabling practical quantum repeater implementations with current technology.
conclusion: Hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes significantly enhance the performance and feasibility of quantum repeaters, bringing resource-efficient loss-tolerant quantum communications closer to reality.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using doped Clifford circuits requires extensive non-Clifford resources, establishing fundamental lower bounds on the T-count.
motivation: Understanding the minimal non-Clifford resources needed to achieve pseudorandomness is crucial for practical quantum computing and for delineating the power of Clifford circuits.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including the concept of stabilizer entropy and the structure of the Clifford group, to derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates required for random unitary ensembles.
result: They show that to achieve a sufficiently close approximation to the Haar measure, the number of non-Clifford gates must scale extensively with the number of qubits, ruling out subextensive doping.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous resource-theoretic characterization of pseudorandomness in Clifford circuits, highlighting the necessity of extensive non-Clifford resources for quantum advantage in certain tasks.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and experimental demonstrations of various quantum cryptographic primitives using photonic platforms.
result: Provides a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and discusses their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Nonstabilizerness And Error Resilience In Noisy Quantum Circuits
authors: Fabian Ballar Trigueros And José Antonio Marín Guzmán
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Ballar Trigueros and José Antonio Marín Guzmán

We investigate how noise impacts nonstabilizerness—a key resource for quantum advantage—in many-body qubit systems. While noise typically degrades quantum resources, we show that amplitude damping, a nonunital channel, can generate or enhance nonstabilizerness, whereas depolarizing noise provably ca…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240602] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how noise affects nonstabilizerness (magic) in many-body qubit systems, finding that amplitude damping can generate or enhance it while depolarizing noise cannot.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its behavior under noise is poorly understood; understanding this is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze the effect of amplitude damping and depolarizing noise on nonstabilizerness in many-body qubit systems, likely using resource theory and numerical simulations.
result: Amplitude damping, a nonunital channel, can generate or enhance nonstabilizerness, whereas depolarizing noise provably cannot.
conclusion: Noise does not always degrade quantum resources; nonunital noise can be beneficial, which has implications for error resilience and resource generation in quantum circuits.

title: Theory Of Quantum Comb Enhanced Interferometry
authors: Haowei Shi And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Haowei Shi and Quntao Zhuang

Optical frequency combs, named for their comblike peaks in the spectrum, are essential for various sensing applications. As the technology develops, its performance has reached the standard quantum limit dictated by the quantum fluctuations of coherent light field. Quantum combs, with their quantum …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243602] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theory of quantum comb enhanced interferometry, showing how quantum combs can surpass the standard quantum limit for phase estimation.
motivation: Optical frequency combs are essential for sensing but are limited by the standard quantum limit; quantum combs offer a path to enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors formulate a quantum information-theoretic framework for comb-based interferometry, analyzing the quantum Fisher information and optimal measurement strategies.
result: They demonstrate that quantum combs can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in phase estimation, outperforming classical combs.
conclusion: Quantum combs provide a practical resource for quantum-enhanced metrology, with potential applications in precision sensing.

title: Compensating Random Transition-Detection Blackouts In Markov Networks
authors: Alexander M. Maier, Benjamin Häsler, And Udo Seifert
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander M. Maier, Benjamin Häsler, and Udo Seifert

In Markov networks, measurement blackouts with unknown frequency compromise observations such that thermodynamic quantities can no longer be inferred reliably. In particular, the observed currents neither discern equilibrium from nonequilibrium nor can they be used in extant estimators of entropy pr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 247101] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper addresses how to infer thermodynamic quantities from Markov networks when random measurement blackouts occur, proposing a method to compensate for missing data.
motivation: Measurement blackouts in Markov networks prevent reliable inference of thermodynamic quantities like entropy production, hindering the detection of nonequilibrium behavior.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to estimate currents and entropy production from incomplete observations by leveraging the network's Markov property and statistical inference techniques.
result: They demonstrate that even with random blackouts, it is possible to distinguish equilibrium from nonequilibrium and accurately estimate entropy production using their compensation method.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for analyzing thermodynamic processes in systems with intermittent measurements, extending the applicability of stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Entanglement Transition In Unitary System-Bath Dynamics
authors: Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, And Dario Poletti
abstract:
Author(s): Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, and Dario Poletti

The evolution of a system coupled to baths is commonly described by a master equation that, in the long-time limit, yields a steady-state density matrix. However, when the same evolution is unraveled into quantum trajectories, it is possible to observe a transition in the scaling of entanglement wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240401] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Unraveling system-bath dynamics into quantum trajectories reveals an entanglement transition in the steady state.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement behaves in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors study a system coupled to baths using a master equation and analyze the entanglement scaling of quantum trajectories in the steady state.
result: They observe a transition in the entanglement entropy scaling from area-law to volume-law as a function of system parameters.
conclusion: The entanglement transition in open systems provides insight into the interplay between unitary dynamics and dissipation, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and information.

title: Anticoncentration And State Design Of Doped Real Clifford Circuits And Tensor Networks
authors: Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, And Xhek Turkeshi
abstract:
Author(s): Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, and Xhek Turkeshi

We investigate the statistical properties of orthogonal, or real, Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources. By developing the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, we derive the exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states, identifying a different universality cl…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062446] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anticoncentration and state design properties of real Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources, using Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of random quantum circuits is crucial for quantum advantage and complexity theory; here the focus is on real Clifford circuits which are experimentally relevant but less studied.
method: The authors develop the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group and derive exact overlap distributions of real stabilizer states, analyzing the emergence of approximate state designs under magic and imaginary doping.
result: They identify a different universality class for real Clifford circuits compared to standard complex Clifford circuits, and characterize the anticoncentration behavior and state design order as a function of doping.
conclusion: Real Clifford circuits with sufficient non-Clifford resources can achieve anticoncentration and form approximate state designs, with implications for quantum advantage experiments and tensor network simulations.

title: Remote Nonreciprocal Optical-microwave Entanglement And One-way Steering Via Parametric Amplification
authors: Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, And Hao Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, and Hao Xiong

We propose a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between spatially separated optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification. Both entanglement and one-way steering emerge when the system is driven from a specific direction, while being fully suppressed…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063730] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification in a hybrid system.
motivation: To achieve directional quantum correlations between disparate frequency modes, which is important for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Uses parametric amplification in a cavity optomechanical system with a nonlinear crystal to create nonreciprocal entanglement and steering between optical and microwave fields.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement and one-way steering emerge only when the system is driven from a specific direction, and are suppressed otherwise.
conclusion: The scheme provides a way to control quantum correlations directionally, with potential applications in quantum communication and hybrid quantum networks.

title: Almost Sure Minimality Of The Set Of Experiments With Classical Kirkwood-Dirac Representations
authors: Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan de Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, And David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan De Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, and David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur

A central problem in quantum information is determining quantum-classical boundaries. In the quasiprobability framework, a state is called classical if it is represented by a quasiprobability distribution that is positive, and thus a probability distribution. In recent years, the Kirkwood-Dirac (KD)…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062215] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the set of quantum experiments with classical Kirkwood-Dirac representations is almost surely minimal, establishing a sharp quantum-classical boundary.
motivation: Determining when a quantum state admits a classical probabilistic representation is a central problem in quantum foundations and information. The Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability provides a framework to study this boundary.
method: The authors use measure-theoretic arguments and random matrix theory to show that for almost all choices of measurements, the set of states with positive KD distribution is minimal (i.e., only states that are simultaneously classical in all bases).
result: They prove that the set of experiments (pairs of orthonormal bases) yielding a nontrivial set of KD-classical states has measure zero, implying that generic experiments have only trivial classical states.
conclusion: The work sharpens the understanding of quantum-classical demarcation in the KD framework, with implications for quantum contextuality and nonclassicality.

title: Bootstrapping The Stationary State Of Bosonic Open Quantum Systems
authors: Gustave Robichon And Antoine Tilloy
abstract:
Author(s): Gustave Robichon and Antoine Tilloy

We propose a method to compute expectation values of observables in the stationary state of a (Markovian) bosonic open quantum system. Using a hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations, we obtain finer and finer upper and lower bounds to any expectation value of interest. The bounds are rigorous, robust…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062440] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A method to compute stationary expectation values of bosonic open quantum systems using semidefinite relaxations, providing rigorous bounds.
motivation: Computing stationary states of bosonic open quantum systems is challenging due to infinite Hilbert spaces; existing methods lack rigorous error bounds.
method: The authors formulate a hierarchy of semidefinite programs that yield converging upper and lower bounds on expectation values of observables in the steady state.
result: The method produces rigorous, robust bounds that improve with hierarchy level, demonstrated on examples like the Kerr oscillator.
conclusion: This approach offers a reliable way to characterize stationary states of bosonic open systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and quantum optics.

title: Tighter Asymptotic Key Rates For Intensity-correlated Decoy-state Quantum Key Distribution Via Nonlinear Programming
authors: Matej Pivoluska And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Matej Pivoluska and Mateus Araújo

Decoy-state QKD with phase-randomized weak coherent pulses is typically analyzed assuming independent, precisely prepared intensities. Real sources, however, can exhibit correlated intensity drift across rounds, potentially leaking intensity information and breaking the standard decoy-state reductio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062441] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Improves asymptotic key rate bounds for decoy-state QKD with intensity correlations using nonlinear programming.
motivation: Real QKD sources have correlated intensity drifts that leak information and break standard decoy-state security proofs, so tighter bounds are needed.
method: Formulates the key rate optimization as a nonlinear programming problem that accounts for intensity correlations across rounds.
result: Obtains significantly tighter asymptotic key rates compared to previous analyses that assumed independent intensities.
conclusion: The nonlinear programming approach provides more realistic security bounds for practical decoy-state QKD systems with correlated sources.

title: Geometric Invariants Of Quantum Metrology
authors: Christopher Wilson, John Drew Wilson, Luke Coffman, Shah Saad Alam, And Murray J. Holland
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Wilson, John Drew Wilson, Luke Coffman, Shah Saad Alam, and Murray J. Holland

We establish a conservation law for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) expressed as follows; when the QFIM is constructed from a set of observables closed under commutation, i.e., a Lie algebra, the spectrum of the QFIM is invariant under unitary dynamics generated by these same operators.…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063725] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a conservation law for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) when constructed from a Lie algebra, showing its spectrum is invariant under unitary dynamics.
motivation: Quantum Fisher information is central to quantum metrology, but its behavior under dynamics was not fully understood; this work provides a geometric invariant that simplifies analysis.
method: The authors consider the QFIM built from observables forming a Lie algebra and prove that its spectrum is invariant under unitary evolution generated by the same algebra, using algebraic and information-geometric techniques.
result: The spectrum of the QFIM is conserved under such dynamics, leading to a geometric invariant that can be used to bound metrological performance.
conclusion: This invariant provides a powerful tool for analyzing quantum metrology protocols and may have implications for optimal sensing and parameter estimation.

title: Limitations Of Quantum Measurements And Operations Of Scattering Type Under The Energy Conservation Law
authors: Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, And Masahiro Hotta
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, and Masahiro Hotta

It is important to improve the accuracy of quantum measurements and operations both in engineering and fundamental physics. It is known, however, that the achievable accuracy of measurements and unitary operations is generally limited by conservation laws according to the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062214] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental limits on quantum measurements and operations of scattering type under energy conservation, extending the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem.
motivation: Improving accuracy of quantum measurements and operations is crucial for both engineering and fundamental physics, but conservation laws impose fundamental limitations.
method: The authors analyze scattering-type measurements and operations, applying the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem and developing new bounds based on energy conservation.
result: They obtain trade-off relations between the accuracy of measurements/operations and the energy uncertainty of the apparatus, generalizing previous results.
conclusion: Energy conservation fundamentally constrains the achievable accuracy of quantum measurements and operations, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Qudit Encoding In Rydberg-blockaded Arrays Of Atoms
authors: Achille Robert And Tom Bienaimé
abstract:
Author(s): Achille Robert and Tom Bienaimé

We propose a protocol to realize arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on a qudit encoded in the collective dressed states of a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms. This system is isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model and acts as a multilevel Rydberg superatom whose nonlinear s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062614] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for qudit encoding and universal control using collective dressed states in a Rydberg-blockaded atomic array, isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model.
motivation: Qudits offer advantages over qubits in quantum information processing, but their realization in atomic platforms is challenging. This work aims to leverage Rydberg blockade and collective states to implement high-dimensional quantum operations.
method: The protocol uses a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms, where the collective dressed states form a multilevel superatom. By driving the system with external fields, arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on the qudit are achieved, exploiting the nonlinear spectrum of the Jaynes-Cummings model.
result: The authors demonstrate that the system is isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model, enabling full qudit control. They show explicit pulse sequences for state preparation and gate operations, with numerical simulations confirming high fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a feasible route to qudit-based quantum computing in Rydberg atom arrays, combining the scalability of neutral atoms with the advantages of higher-dimensional encoding.

title: Photon-mediated Hybridization And Dissipative Transport In A cavity-QED Ring-acceptor Architecture
authors: Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, And Sarben Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, and Sarben Sarkar

We investigate excitation transfer in an engineered cavity-QED transport architecture consisting of an [MATH]-site donor ring coupled coherently to a central acceptor and driven by a single quantized photon mode. The system evolves under a Lindblad master equation including spontaneous loss and pure de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063721] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies excitation transfer in a cavity-QED ring-acceptor architecture driven by a single photon mode, using a Lindblad master equation to model dissipative transport.
motivation: Understanding photon-mediated energy transport in engineered quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing and light-harvesting applications.
method: The authors model a donor ring coupled to a central acceptor, driven by a quantized photon mode, and solve the Lindblad master equation including spontaneous loss and pure dephasing.
result: They find that photon-mediated hybridization leads to efficient and controllable excitation transfer, with dissipative effects playing a key role in transport dynamics.
conclusion: The cavity-QED architecture provides a tunable platform for studying quantum transport and may inspire new designs for quantum networks or energy transfer devices.

title: Sensitivity Enhancement In Superconducting-qubit Magnetometry Via Two-level Systems
authors: Azat Gubaydullin, Vladimir Slepnev, Valerii Vinokur, And Florian Neukart
abstract:
Author(s): Azat Gubaydullin, Vladimir Slepnev, Valerii Vinokur, and Florian Neukart

We study quantum magnetometry based on phase-estimation algorithms in a sensor formed by a superconducting qubit coupled to a two-level system (TLS). Using Ramsey interferometry with single-shot binary readout, we construct a precomputed calibration pattern [MATH] and implement…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224522] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A superconducting qubit coupled to a two-level system is used as a quantum magnetometer with enhanced sensitivity via phase-estimation algorithms.
motivation: To improve the sensitivity of quantum magnetometry by leveraging the interaction between a superconducting qubit and a TLS, which can enhance the sensor's performance.
method: The authors use Ramsey interferometry with single-shot binary readout and a precomputed calibration pattern to implement phase-estimation algorithms on a superconducting qubit-TLS system.
result: The TLS-coupled qubit sensor achieves enhanced sensitivity compared to a bare qubit, demonstrating the utility of TLS for magnetometry.
conclusion: Superconducting qubits coupled to TLSs offer a promising platform for high-sensitivity quantum magnetometry, with potential applications in quantum sensing.

title: Minimal-dissipation Learning For Energy-based Models
authors: Jeff Hnybida And Simon Verret
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Hnybida and Simon Verret

We show that the bias of the approximate maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) objective of a persistent chain energy-based model (EBM) is precisely equal to the thermodynamic excess work of an overdamped Langevin dynamical system. We then answer the question of whether such a model can be trained wit…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065306] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the bias in maximum-likelihood estimation for energy-based models equals thermodynamic excess work, and explores minimal-dissipation training.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost of training energy-based models and to find training protocols that minimize dissipation.
method: The authors map the persistent chain EBM training to an overdamped Langevin system and derive the bias as excess work, then propose a minimal-dissipation learning approach.
result: The bias of approximate MLE is exactly the thermodynamic excess work, and minimal-dissipation training can reduce this cost.
conclusion: Energy-based model training can be understood and optimized using thermodynamic principles, bridging machine learning and nonequilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Statistical-gauge Geometry
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, can be hard to expose because local currents are distributional and equal-time commutators may contain anomaly-like contact terms. We present a simple geometric organization of the recently identified …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework for organizing exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, using a statistical-gauge geometry.
motivation: Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems are often hard to expose due to distributional local currents and anomaly-like contact terms. A systematic geometric organization is needed to clarify these constraints.
method: The authors develop a geometric approach based on a statistical-gauge structure, which organizes the equilibrium constraints (sum rules, Ward identities) in a unified manner, likely using differential geometry or gauge theory concepts.
result: The paper presents a simple geometric organization of the recently identified constraints, providing a clear framework for understanding and deriving exact equilibrium properties.
conclusion: The geometric formulation offers a powerful tool for analyzing quantum many-body systems at equilibrium, with potential applications to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and information-theoretic bounds.

title: Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Nonreciprocally Interacting Particles And Fields
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Nonreciprocal interactions that violate Newton's law “actio = reactio” are ubiquitous in nature and are currently intensively investigated in active matter, chemical reaction networks, population dynamics, and many other fields. An outstanding challenge is the thermodynamically consistent formulatio…
