[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064136] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic thermodynamic framework for nonreciprocally interacting particles and fields, deriving fluctuation theorems and entropy production bounds.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions are common in active matter and biological systems, but a consistent thermodynamic description was lacking.
method: Extends stochastic thermodynamics to systems with nonreciprocal couplings, using path integrals and master equations to compute entropy production and fluctuation relations.
result: Derives generalized fluctuation theorems and shows that nonreciprocity leads to additional entropy production terms beyond standard forms.
conclusion: The framework provides a thermodynamically consistent way to model nonreciprocal systems, with implications for active matter and information processing.

title: Gradient Scalability And Taylor Surrogation Of Quantum Cost Landscapes
authors: Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, And Aurelien Lucchi
abstract:
Author(s): Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, and Aurelien Lucchi

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing, yet they face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in the system size. Recent conjectures suggest that avoiding barren plateaus might inherently lead to clas…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023325] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the scalability of gradients in variational quantum algorithms and proposes a Taylor surrogation method to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially. Understanding and mitigating this issue is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze gradient scaling in VQAs and introduce a Taylor surrogation technique that approximates the cost function to improve gradient estimation.
result: They show that the proposed method can alleviate barren plateaus and maintain gradient magnitudes that scale polynomially with system size for certain ansätze.
conclusion: Taylor surrogation offers a practical approach to enhance trainability of VQAs, though its effectiveness depends on the ansatz and problem structure.

title: Indefinite Causal Order In Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, And Tim J. Bartley
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, and Tim J. Bartley

Indefinite causal order (ICO) has the potential to be a new resource for quantum information processing. In most of its experiments, ICO has been investigated in a photonic platform. Here, we investigate ICO in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system composed of two cavities. Our results show that I…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023295] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates indefinite causal order (ICO) in a cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) system, demonstrating a new platform for ICO beyond photonic systems.
motivation: ICO is a potential resource for quantum information processing, but most experiments have been limited to photonic platforms. Exploring ICO in other physical systems, such as cavity QED, could enable new applications and insights.
method: The authors propose a cavity QED setup with two cavities and analyze the conditions for achieving ICO using the quantum switch, modeling the system with appropriate Hamiltonians and master equations.
result: They show that ICO can be realized in cavity QED, with the ability to control the causal order via cavity parameters and coupling strengths.
conclusion: Cavity QED provides a viable platform for ICO experiments, potentially offering advantages in scalability and integration with other quantum technologies.

title: Efficient And Simple Gibbs State Preparation Of The Two-dimensional Toric Code Via Duality To Classical Ising Chains
authors: Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, And Ángela Capel
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, and Ángela Capel

We introduce the notion of polynomial-depth duality transformations, which relates two sets of operator algebras through a conjugation by a poly-depth quantum circuit, and make use of this to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for a variety of interesting quantum Hamiltonians as they are poly-depth …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023277] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces polynomial-depth duality transformations to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for the 2D toric code, leveraging a duality to classical Ising chains.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states of quantum Hamiltonians is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics, but efficient methods for topologically ordered systems like the toric code are lacking.
method: The authors define polynomial-depth duality transformations that map the toric code Hamiltonian to a classical Ising chain via a shallow quantum circuit, enabling efficient Gibbs sampling using classical algorithms.
result: They demonstrate that the Gibbs state of the 2D toric code can be prepared with polynomial resources, and the method extends to other Hamiltonians with similar dualities.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to Gibbs state preparation for certain quantum systems, bridging quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Harvesting Chemical Power From Cyclic Environments
authors: Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, And Christoph A. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, and Christoph A. Weber

Life relies on a sophisticated metabolic molecular machinery that turns over high-energy molecules to evolve complex macromolecules and assemblies. At the molecular origin of life, such machinery was absent, implying the need for simple yet robust physical mechanisms to harvest energy from the envir…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023289] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a simple physical mechanism for harvesting chemical energy from cyclic environmental fluctuations, relevant to the origin of life.
motivation: To understand how early life could harvest energy without complex molecular machinery, by exploiting cyclic environmental changes.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of a chemical system driven by a cyclic external field, analyzing energy extraction using stochastic thermodynamics.
result: They show that cyclic environments can power chemical reactions, enabling the synthesis of high-energy molecules through a ratchet-like mechanism.
conclusion: Cyclic environmental fluctuations provide a robust and simple mechanism for chemical energy harvesting, which may have been crucial for the emergence of life.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis entangled states are used for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, suppressing common-mode noise for scalable sensor networks.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. Entangled states can enhance sensitivity, but are fragile; Lieb-Mattis states offer intrinsic noise insensitivity.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of two spin ensembles with opposite magnetization, to perform differential phase measurements. They analyze the sensitivity and robustness to common-mode noise using quantum metrology techniques.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling for differential phase estimation while being immune to common-mode phase noise, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical and robust platform for quantum-enhanced differential sensing, enabling scalable quantum sensor networks in realistic noisy conditions.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are useful for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a combination of laser pulses and engineered interactions to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution over fiber.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom components but suffers from limited secret key rates and security proofs. The authors aim to overcome these limitations using discrete modulation and composable security analysis.
method: The protocol uses a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) on coherent states, combined with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization of the secret key rate.
result: They achieve a secret key rate of several Mbps over 50 km of fiber, with rigorous composable security against collective attacks, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD demonstrations.
conclusion: The work shows that discrete-modulated CV-QKD can achieve high rates with practical security, bringing quantum key distribution closer to real-world deployment in metropolitan networks.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating a key capability for hybrid quantum systems.
conclusion: This technique enables new possibilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly in hybrid setups.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization dynamics using experimental techniques and theoretical modeling, focusing on multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They reveal the mechanisms of transmon ionization, showing how qubits transition to highly excited states through multiphoton processes.
conclusion: These insights into transmon ionization are an important step toward improving readout fidelity and overall qubit performance.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubits, challenging error correction even with shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They find that radiation induces spatially and temporally correlated phase errors that persist despite state-of-the-art shielding, degrading error correction performance.
conclusion: New mitigation strategies beyond passive shielding are needed to protect superconducting qubits from radiation-induced correlated errors.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems based on measurement-adapted time-coarse graining that captures observable dynamics at the resolution of measurement channels.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a reduction technique that preserves only the dynamics relevant to a given measurement is needed.
method: The authors introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, which coarse-grains time according to the temporal resolution of measurement channels, and derive a reduced master equation.
result: The method accurately reproduces the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system while significantly reducing computational cost.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining is an effective model reduction tool for open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to decompose a state, and derive its properties using symplectic geometry and phase-space representations.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it dictates the minimal number of non-Gaussian elements needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful tool for quantifying non-Gaussian resources, with implications for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying sources of decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with stable spectra are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral diffusion and decoherence limit performance. Understanding these mechanisms is essential for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study single erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, performing spectroscopy and noise analysis to characterize spectral instability and decoherence.
result: They identify specific origins of spectral instability and decoherence, providing insights into the physical processes affecting emitter performance.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of more stable cavity-enhanced single-photon emitters, advancing quantum networking and computation platforms.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Characterizing unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model orders, enabling fast and scalable estimation.
result: The method accurately identifies the number and parameters of spin baths in simulated and experimental NV center data, and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation tasks, with potential applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low atom loss remains challenging. EIT offers a way to perform nondestructive imaging and continuous loading.
method: The authors apply electromagnetically induced transparency to achieve nondestructive imaging of atom arrays, and use it to continuously load atoms into the array while maintaining high fidelity.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays, demonstrating the effectiveness of EIT for these tasks in finite magnetic fields.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading is a powerful technique for neutral-atom arrays, enabling continuous operation and high-fidelity state detection, which is important for quantum information processing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: To realize compact, scalable quantum security devices by integrating self-testing quantum randomness expansion on a photonic chip.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a device-independent quantum random number generation protocol using entangled photon pairs and self-testing.
result: The chip successfully generates certified randomness with high rates, showing that self-testing protocols can be implemented on an integrated photonic platform.
conclusion: This work paves the way for production-scale quantum security devices by demonstrating that complex quantum protocols can be miniaturized and integrated.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics using master equations.
result: They find that photon blockade strengthens with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission, even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper improves variational counterdiabatic driving for quantum control using weighted actions and computer algebra, enhancing fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique to speed up quantum adiabatic processes, but exact implementation is challenging; variational methods offer approximations. The authors aim to boost fidelity of these approximations.
method: They introduce a weighted action approach combined with computer algebra to optimize variational counterdiabatic driving, deriving better control protocols.
result: The new method yields higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving, demonstrated on example systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a readily available upgrade to current quantum control methods, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, which demands amplifiers with high bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing their parameters to achieve enhanced bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers demonstrate improved performance metrics, enabling simultaneous amplification and transduction of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These enhanced Josephson mixers are promising components for scalable quantum information processing and quantum networks.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear definitions and quantitative measures of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria and numerical methods to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using tools from many-body physics and topological quantum computation.
result: They provide a rigorous framework to distinguish true Majorana bound states from trivial Andreev bound states, and quantify how interactions affect their protection and non-Abelian properties.
conclusion: The work establishes practical benchmarks for identifying and characterizing Majorana bound states in interacting systems, guiding experimental efforts toward topological qubits.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods often scale poorly with system size or are not tailored to correlated noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of k-local decoupling sequences.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits and effectively cancel spatially correlated noise up to k-body interactions.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical, scalable noise mitigation for quantum devices.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for optimizing training.
method: The authors analyze noisy parametrized quantum circuits using tools from statistical learning theory and quantum information, deriving bounds on the variance of the loss function in terms of circuit expressivity and noise parameters.
result: They show that noise can reduce the variance of the loss function, potentially alleviating barren plateaus, but also introduces a trade-off between expressivity and trainability. Quantitative estimates are provided for common noise models.
conclusion: The results offer a principled framework for designing noise-resilient variational algorithms and suggest that moderate noise can be beneficial for trainability, guiding experimental implementations.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that combine deterministic and randomized Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation theory and phase estimation error analysis.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation, with rigorous error bounds.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and provably efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, bringing quantum chemistry simulations closer to feasibility.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause back-action that destroys quantum information; a nondemolition readout is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize disturbance, using real-time feedback on a silicon spin qudit.
result: They achieve a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and measurement-induced errors, outperforming standard approaches.
conclusion: Adaptive readout protocols can significantly enhance the nondemolition nature of quantum measurements, benefiting qudit-based quantum processors across various platforms.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrix under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength. The spectral properties exhibit universal features.
conclusion: The work provides a simple mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations improves simulation accuracy sevenfold for variational algorithms.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical modeling.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms compared to standard noise models.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, enabling better error mitigation strategies.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the emergence of thermodynamics in many-body systems.
method: The authors develop a framework based on process tensors and projected ensembles to probe chaos through repeated interventions on a quantum system.
result: They show that the projected ensemble approach can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics and provides a unified perspective on existing chaos diagnostics.
conclusion: The method offers a new tool for analyzing quantum chaos, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and practical implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer advantages in quantum communication, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution, but require a unified overview of recent developments.
method: The paper surveys CV quantum communication protocols, including CV-QKD, measurement-device-independent CV-QKD, and continuous-variable entanglement distribution, and discusses security proofs, practical implementations, and experimental progress.
result: CV quantum communication is now as mature as discrete-variable approaches, with demonstrated long-distance QKD, high secret key rates, and integration with classical networks.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and promising platform for practical quantum networks, with ongoing work needed to improve distance and security under realistic conditions.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with focus on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review and classify universal behavior using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to symmetry and topology.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory in nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and predictive computational methods can guide the design of better qubits.
method: The paper reviews ab initio cluster expansion techniques to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion methods can reliably predict coherence times for many qubit types, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming reliable, aiding the development of solid-state spin qubits for quantum technologies.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, as classical gravity cannot generate entanglement between quantum probes, providing a test for quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks using quantum information concepts (entanglement, nonlocality) and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement.
result: Several feasible experiments are identified that could detect gravitationally induced entanglement, constraining theories of gravity.
conclusion: Quantum information methods offer a concrete path to experimentally test the quantum nature of gravity, with promising tabletop-scale proposals.

title: Quantum State Preparation Without Coherent Arithmetic
authors: Sam Mcardle, András Gilyén, And Mario Berta
abstract:
Author(s): Sam McArdle, András Gilyén, and Mario Berta

We introduce a versatile method for preparing a quantum state whose amplitudes are given by some known function. Unlike existing approaches, our method does not require handcrafted reversible arithmetic circuits, or quantum table reads, to encode the function values. Instead, we use a template quant…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240603] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing quantum states with amplitudes given by a known function without coherent arithmetic, using a template quantum state and classical post-processing.
motivation: Existing state preparation methods require complex reversible arithmetic circuits or quantum table lookups, which are resource-intensive. This work aims to reduce the quantum resource cost.
method: The authors propose preparing a template quantum state that is independent of the target function, then applying a classical post-processing step to adjust the amplitudes via a simple quantum circuit that does not require coherent arithmetic.
result: The method achieves a reduction in T-gate count and overall circuit depth compared to previous approaches, while maintaining high fidelity for a class of functions.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical alternative for state preparation in quantum algorithms, particularly when the function is known and can be efficiently computed classically.

title: Universal Two-Excitation Scattering In Two-Dimensional Subwavelength Atomic Arrays
authors: Yidan Wang (王艺丹), Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, Valentin Walther, And Susanne F. Yelin
abstract:
Author(s): Yidan Wang (王艺丹), Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, Valentin Walther, and Susanne F. Yelin

Subwavelength atomic arrays are a leading platform for engineering strong light-matter interactions, presenting exciting opportunities for quantum science. However, a full understanding of their multiexcitation dynamics remains a significant challenge. In this Letter, we uncover a remarkable univers…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243603] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals universal two-excitation scattering behavior in subwavelength atomic arrays, showing that the scattering matrix depends only on the number of atoms and not on the array geometry.
motivation: Understanding multiexcitation dynamics in subwavelength atomic arrays is crucial for quantum science applications, but a full theoretical description has been lacking.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on the coupled-dipole model and analyze two-excitation scattering in one- and two-dimensional arrays, deriving universal properties of the scattering matrix.
result: They find that the two-excitation scattering matrix is universal for arrays with more than a few atoms, independent of the specific lattice structure, and demonstrate this universality through analytical and numerical calculations.
conclusion: The universality simplifies the description of multiexcitation dynamics and suggests that subwavelength atomic arrays can serve as robust platforms for quantum information processing and nonlinear optics.

title: State- Versus Reaction-Based Information Processing In Biochemical Networks
authors: Anne-Lena Moor, Age Tjalma, Manuel Reinhardt, Pieter Rein Ten Wolde, And Christoph Zechner
abstract:
Author(s): Anne-Lena Moor, Age Tjalma, Manuel Reinhardt, Pieter Rein ten Wolde, and Christoph Zechner

Trajectory mutual information is frequently used to quantify information transfer in biochemical systems. Tractable solutions of the trajectory mutual information can be obtained via the widely used linear-noise approximation (LNA) using Gaussian channel theory. This approach is expected to be accur…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 248401] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes information processing in biochemical networks using trajectory mutual information and the linear-noise approximation, revealing that reaction-based information is more robust than state-based information.
motivation: Understanding how biochemical networks process information is crucial for systems biology, but existing measures like trajectory mutual information are often approximated using Gaussian channel theory, whose validity for nonlinear systems is unclear.
method: The authors compare state-based and reaction-based information measures using the linear-noise approximation (LNA) and exact stochastic simulations for a model of a biochemical network.
result: They find that reaction-based information (mutual information between reaction events) is more robust to nonlinearities and provides a more reliable measure of information transfer than state-based information.
conclusion: Reaction-based information processing is a more appropriate framework for quantifying information flow in biochemical networks, especially when nonlinearities are present.

title: Parent Hamiltonians For Stabilizer Quantum Many-Body Scars
authors: Shane Dooley
abstract:
Author(s): Shane Dooley

Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) have attracted considerable interest due to their role in weak ergodicity breaking in many-body systems. We present a general construction that embeds stabilizer states as QMBS of local Hamiltonians. The method relies on a notion of factorizability of Pauli strings on …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240402] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A general construction to embed stabilizer states as quantum many-body scars in local Hamiltonians, using factorizability of Pauli strings.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) are a novel mechanism for weak ergodicity breaking; constructing explicit parent Hamiltonians for known scar states is important for understanding and engineering such systems.
method: The authors define a notion of factorizability of Pauli strings and use it to build local Hamiltonians for which given stabilizer states are exact eigenstates with low entanglement, i.e., scars.
result: They demonstrate the construction for several examples, including the AKLT chain and the PXP model, showing that stabilizer states can be embedded as QMBS.
conclusion: This provides a systematic way to generate Hamiltonians with desired scar states, potentially useful for quantum information tasks like state preparation and memory.

title: Non-Hermitian Cavity Magnomechanics With $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry-related Asymmetric Transparency
authors: Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, And Kashif Ammar Yasir
abstract:
Author(s): Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, and Kashif Ammar Yasir

We investigate magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling. The setup consists of a microwave cavity mode coupled to magnons in a single-crystal yttrium iron garnet sphere, where the magnon mode is further hybridized w…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063522] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Investigates non-Hermitian cavity magnomechanics with PT-symmetry-related asymmetric transparency.
motivation: To explore magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with non-Hermitian coupling, which is relevant for quantum information processing and sensing.
method: Theoretical analysis of a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling, involving a microwave cavity mode coupled to magnons in a YIG sphere.
result: Demonstrates PT-symmetry-related asymmetric transparency and related phenomena.
conclusion: Provides insights into non-Hermitian physics in hybrid quantum systems, potentially useful for quantum transducers and magnon-based devices.

title: Nonreciprocal Universal Photon Blockade In An Asymmetrical Cavity
authors: Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, And Yaping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, and Yaping Yang

Inspired by the distinctive properties of universal photon blockade (UPB), we propose a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity to achieve quantum nonreciprocity. Through theoretical analysis, we establish direction-dependent optimal conditions for perfect UPB in weak-driving limita…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063729] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity to achieve nonreciprocal universal photon blockade.
motivation: Universal photon blockade (UPB) is a key effect for quantum information processing, but achieving nonreciprocal behavior is challenging. This work aims to realize direction-dependent UPB using an asymmetrical cavity.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity, deriving optimal conditions for perfect UPB under weak driving. They use quantum master equation and input-output formalism.
result: They find that nonreciprocal UPB can be achieved with high contrast, and the direction of the blockade can be controlled by system parameters.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a way to realize quantum nonreciprocity at the single-photon level, which is useful for quantum networks and information processing.

title: Effects Of Static Dc Electric-field Orientation On Two-photon Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Rob Behary, William Torg, Mykhailo Vorobiov, Nicolas Destefano, Adam Vernon, Charles T. Fancher, Neel Malvania, Eugeniy E. Mikhailov, Seth Aubin, And Irina Novikova
abstract:
Author(s): Rob Behary, William Torg, Mykhailo Vorobiov, Nicolas DeStefano, Adam Vernon, Charles T. Fancher, Neel Malvania, Eugeniy E. Mikhailov, Seth Aubin, and Irina Novikova

We examine the influence of a static dc electric field on electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) resonances that involve highly excited Rydberg states. Our focus is on how these resonances are altered when the relative orientation between the laser polarization and the external electric-fiel…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062619] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the orientation of a static DC electric field relative to laser polarization affects two-photon Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) resonances.
motivation: Understanding the influence of electric field orientation on Rydberg EIT is important for applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems where Rydberg atoms are used as electric field sensors or interfaces.
method: The authors experimentally measure EIT spectra in a rubidium vapor cell with highly excited Rydberg states while varying the direction of an applied DC electric field relative to the laser polarization, and compare with theoretical models.
result: They find that the EIT resonance amplitude and linewidth depend strongly on the field orientation, consistent with Stark shift and mixing of Rydberg states, and demonstrate control over the EIT response.
conclusion: The orientation of the DC field is a critical parameter for optimizing Rydberg EIT-based devices, and the results provide guidelines for designing electric field sensors and quantum transducers.

title: Application And Quantum Properties Of Superpositions Of Oppositely Squeezed States
authors: Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, And Kae Nemoto
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, and Kae Nemoto

We show that superpositions of oppositely squeezed states—non-Gaussian Schrödinger-cat-like states—exhibit enhanced nonclassical features and provide an entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime. These states possess photon-number structures distinct from conventional coherent-state cat s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063728] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states are shown to exhibit enhanced nonclassical features and entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime.
motivation: To explore non-Gaussian Schrödinger-cat-like states that may offer advantages for quantum information processing, particularly in continuous-variable systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the photon-number structure and nonclassical properties of superpositions of oppositely squeezed states, and study their entanglement advantage in a specific protocol.
result: These states display enhanced nonclassical features and provide an entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime compared to conventional cat states.
conclusion: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states are promising non-Gaussian resources for quantum information tasks, especially when squeezing is limited.

title: Optimal Control Of Open-quantum-system Dynamics Predicted By Long Short-term Memory
authors: Jun-Dong Zhong And Zhao-Ming Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Dong Zhong and Zhao-Ming Wang

The realization of high-fidelity quantum control is crucial for quantum information processing, particularly in noisy environments where control strategies must simultaneously achieve precise manipulation and effective noise suppression. Conventional optimal control designs typically require numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062442] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Uses LSTM neural networks to predict optimal control pulses for open quantum systems, achieving high-fidelity state preparation under noise.
motivation: Conventional optimal control for open quantum systems is computationally expensive; machine learning offers a faster alternative for designing robust control pulses.
method: Trains a long short-term memory (LSTM) network on numerically optimized control pulses to predict new pulses for target operations, incorporating Lindblad master equation dynamics.
result: The LSTM-predicted pulses achieve fidelities comparable to numerically optimized pulses for single-qubit gates and state preparation in noisy environments.
conclusion: Machine learning can efficiently generate high-fidelity control pulses for open quantum systems, reducing computational cost while maintaining performance.

title: Enhancing Collective Spin Squeezing Via One-axis-twisting Echo Control Of Individual Atoms
authors: Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, And Yanhong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, and Yanhong Xiao

Spin squeezing generated via interatom entanglement in multilevel atomic ensembles provides a powerful resource for quantum-enhanced metrology. Existing schemes that harness internal atomic degrees of freedom to boost squeezing typically encode the collective squeezing in complex superpositions of m…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062809] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a one-axis-twisting echo control method to enhance collective spin squeezing in multilevel atomic ensembles, improving metrological gain.
motivation: Existing spin squeezing schemes using internal atomic degrees of freedom suffer from limited squeezing due to decoherence and complexity. The authors aim to develop a robust protocol that enhances squeezing while maintaining experimental feasibility.
method: The authors introduce a one-axis-twisting echo control sequence that refocuses inhomogeneous broadening and decoherence in multilevel atomic ensembles, effectively generating enhanced collective spin squeezing through interatom entanglement.
result: The proposed protocol achieves significantly higher squeezing levels compared to standard one-axis-twisting schemes, with improved robustness against experimental imperfections.
conclusion: The one-axis-twisting echo control provides a practical and effective method for generating strong spin squeezing in atomic ensembles, with potential applications in quantum-enhanced metrology.

title: Increasing Entanglement Concentration And The Role Of Measurement Imaginarity
authors: Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, And Debasis Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, and Debasis Sarkar

The role of complex numbers in quantum theory extends beyond mathematical convenience, having recently been formalized as a resource under the framework of the resource theory of imaginarity. Operationally, imaginarity translates into using more resources in linear optical setups. In this work, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062439] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how the imaginarity of measurements affects entanglement concentration, showing that using complex-valued measurements can increase the yield of maximally entangled states from partially entangled ones.
motivation: Understanding the role of complex numbers in quantum theory as a resource, and exploring whether imaginarity can enhance entanglement manipulation tasks.
method: The authors develop a resource-theoretic framework for measurement imaginarity and apply it to the task of entanglement concentration, deriving bounds and protocols that exploit imaginarity.
result: They find that measurements with non-zero imaginarity can increase the achievable entanglement concentration yield compared to real-valued measurements, establishing a quantitative advantage.
conclusion: Imaginarity in measurements is a useful resource for entanglement concentration, highlighting the operational significance of complex numbers in quantum information processing.

title: Demonstration Of The Universal Intrinsic Higher-rank Spin Tensor Hall Effect With A Trapped Ion
authors: Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, And Yiheng Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, and Yiheng Lin

The spin Hall effect enables pure spin-current generation without charge transport. Notably, its intrinsic contribution, originating from spin-orbit coupling, can exhibit universal values that are robust against parameter fluctuations. Recent extensions of this effect to high-spin systems predict ri…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062616] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a universal intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect using a trapped ion system.
motivation: To realize and characterize higher-rank spin tensor Hall effects in a controlled quantum platform, extending the spin Hall effect to high-spin systems.
method: Trapped ion quantum simulation with engineered spin-orbit coupling to observe the intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect.
result: Observation of universal values of the spin tensor Hall effect that are robust against parameter fluctuations.
conclusion: The trapped ion platform can simulate higher-rank spin Hall effects, providing insights into spin transport in high-spin systems.

title: Tunable Bundle Emissions Of $n$-phonon And Photon-phonon Pairs Via The Barnett Effect
authors: Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, And Zhi-Rong Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, and Zhi-Rong Zhong

We theoretically propose a scheme for the generation of [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions in a cavity magnomechanics system. By utilizing the Barnett effect under resonant driving, [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations can be achieved. Through the system's dissipative…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063722] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a cavity magnomechanics system to generate n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions via the Barnett effect.
motivation: To achieve tunable bundle emissions of phonons and photon-phonon pairs, which are important for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Uses the Barnett effect under resonant driving in a cavity magnomechanics system to induce n-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations, then leverages dissipative dynamics to generate bundle emissions.
result: Demonstrates that n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions can be generated and tuned by controlling system parameters.
conclusion: The scheme provides a new method for generating nonclassical states in hybrid magnomechanical systems, with potential applications in quantum networks and sensing.

title: Emergence Of Prethermal Time-quasicrystalline Order In A Quasiperiodically Driven Noninteracting Spin Chain
authors: Davood Marripour And Jahanfar Abouie
abstract:
Author(s): Davood Marripour and Jahanfar Abouie

We study prethermal time quasicrystalline (TQC) order in a quasiperiodically driven chain of noninteracting spin-1/2 particles. The drive consists of two parts, switched on and off periodically with frequency [MATH]: (i) disordered Ising interactions, with exchange couplings chosen from a symmetr…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214318] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies prethermal time-quasicrystalline order in a quasiperiodically driven noninteracting spin chain, focusing on the interplay between driving and disorder.
motivation: To understand how quasiperiodic driving can stabilize time-crystalline order in noninteracting systems, which is relevant to non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and prethermalization.
method: The authors consider a chain of noninteracting spin-1/2 particles with a quasiperiodic drive consisting of disordered Ising interactions switched on and off periodically. They analyze the dynamics using Floquet theory and compute observables such as magnetization.
result: They find that prethermal time-quasicrystalline order emerges, characterized by subharmonic response and robustness against perturbations, even in the absence of interactions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that quasiperiodic driving can stabilize time-crystalline order in noninteracting systems, extending the understanding of prethermal phases and their thermodynamic properties.

title: Topological And Nontopological Defects From Quantum Reset Dynamics
authors: R. Jafari, Henrik Johannesson, And Sebastian Eggert
abstract:
Author(s): R. Jafari, Henrik Johannesson, and Sebastian Eggert

We analyze mechanisms for universal out-of-equilibrium dynamics near criticality by exploring the effect of randomized quantum resetting (QR) under a linear finite-time drive across, or very close to, an equilibrium quantum critical point. Using the transverse-field Ising chain as a minimal model an…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224312] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies universal out-of-equilibrium dynamics near a quantum critical point under randomized quantum resetting, using the transverse-field Ising chain as a model.
motivation: Understanding non-equilibrium dynamics near criticality is fundamental to quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics; quantum resetting is a novel protocol that may reveal universal behavior.
method: The authors analyze the effect of randomized quantum resetting (QR) under a linear finite-time drive across or near an equilibrium quantum critical point, using the transverse-field Ising chain as a minimal model.
result: They identify mechanisms for universal out-of-equilibrium dynamics, including topological and nontopological defects arising from the resetting process.
conclusion: Quantum resetting provides a new tool to probe and control defect formation in quantum phase transitions, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Open-system Dynamics In Local Lindbladians With Chaotic Spectra
authors: Sanket Chirame And Fiona J. Burnell
abstract:
Author(s): Sanket Chirame and Fiona J. Burnell

We investigate the physical consequences of having a spectrum that satisfies random matrix theory (RMT) for generic Lindbladians, and compare its implications for spatially local and completely random Lindblad dynamics in one spatial dimension. We find that Lindbladians whose spectrum is described b…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224314] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies open quantum systems with Lindbladians whose spectra follow random matrix theory, comparing spatially local and completely random dynamics in 1D.
motivation: Understanding the physical consequences of chaotic spectra in Lindbladians is important for characterizing thermalization and dynamics in open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze Lindbladians with random matrix theory spectral statistics, comparing local and fully random Lindblad dynamics in one spatial dimension.
result: They find that Lindbladians with RMT spectra exhibit distinct dynamical features depending on spatial locality, with implications for thermalization and chaos.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between chaos and locality in open quantum systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and thermalization.

title: Zeeman-like Coupling To Valley Degree Of Freedom In Si-based Spin Qubits
authors: S. A. Jafari, Hendrik Bluhm, And David P. Divincenzo
abstract:
Author(s): S. A. Jafari, Hendrik Bluhm, and David P. DiVincenzo

Increasing the valley splitting in Si-based heterostructures is critical for improving the performance of semiconductor qubits. This paper establishes that the two low-energy conduction band valleys are not independent parabolic bands. Instead, they originate from the X point of the Brillouin zone, …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245204] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a Zeeman-like coupling to the valley degree of freedom in Si-based spin qubits, showing that the two low-energy conduction band valleys are not independent but coupled via a spin-orbit-like interaction.
motivation: Increasing valley splitting in Si-based heterostructures is critical for improving semiconductor qubit performance, and understanding valley coupling is essential for qubit control.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the band structure near the X point of the Brillouin zone, deriving an effective Hamiltonian that captures the valley coupling analogous to Zeeman splitting.
result: They find that the valley states exhibit a coupling that mimics a Zeeman effect, which can be tuned by external fields, providing a new mechanism for qubit manipulation.
conclusion: This work offers a pathway to utilize the valley degree of freedom as a resource for qubit control in silicon spin qubits, potentially enhancing coherence and gate fidelity.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Optimal navigation strategy for a small swimmer in a flow balances accuracy and cost, revealing a trade-off between passive drifting and active swimming.
motivation: Understand how microscopic swimmers can localize near a target despite environmental noise and flow, which is relevant to active matter and biological systems.
method: The authors model a swimmer in a stochastic environment with a flow, using optimal control theory to minimize a cost function that penalizes both distance from target and energy expenditure.
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a trade-off between accuracy (staying close to target) and cost (energy used).
conclusion: Accuracy in localization comes at a thermodynamic cost, illustrating a fundamental principle in information thermodynamics for active agents.

title: Dynamical Typicality In Classical Lattice Systems
authors: Nicolas Nessi And Peter Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Nessi and Peter Reimann

Considering deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables, we show that, if the initial conditions are sampled according to a probability distribution in which the dynamical variables are statistically independent, the temporal evolution of any macroscopic observable is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves dynamical typicality for classical lattice systems, showing that typical initial conditions lead to predictable macroscopic behavior.
motivation: Understanding how macroscopic observables evolve from typical initial conditions is fundamental to statistical mechanics and the foundations of thermodynamics.
method: The authors consider deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous variables and sample initial conditions from a product distribution, then analyze the temporal evolution of macroscopic observables.
result: They show that for any macroscopic observable, the time evolution is essentially the same for almost all initial conditions, i.e., dynamical typicality holds.
conclusion: This result provides a rigorous justification for the use of typicality in classical statistical mechanics, bridging microscopic dynamics and macroscopic predictability.

title: Quantum Dynamical Signatures Of Topological Flow Transitions In Limit Cycle Phases
authors: Alejandro S. Gómez And Javier Del Pino
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro S. Gómez and Javier del Pino

Quantum self-oscillatory phases are ubiquitous in driven-dissipative systems. Classically, each phase is defined by its flow pattern and how stationary sets organize phase space (e.g., fixed points and limit cycles), with transitions triggered by local bifurcations or global basin rearrangements. In…
