[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: They develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the end, allowing for efficient classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: The method significantly reduces the computational cost of simulating magic state preparation, enabling the analysis of larger and more complex protocols.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for designing and verifying magic state preparation protocols, which is important for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of nonequilibrium dynamics in photoexcited Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and photoinduced phase transitions.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium states in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders such as superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators offer a rich platform for exploring quantum matter, but the field is still developing.

title: Theory Of Anomalous Landau-Zener Tunneling Induced By Nonlinear Coupling
authors: Wen-Yuan Wang And Hong-Juan Meng
abstract:

We develop a general theory of Landau-Zener (LZ) tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent, sign-reversible nonlinear coupling, distinguishing it fundamentally from conventional on-site nonlinearity. Through a combination of analytical and phase-space analysis, we show that beyond a c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062218] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops a theory of Landau-Zener tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent nonlinear coupling.
motivation: To understand the effect of nonlinear coupling on Landau-Zener tunneling, which differs from conventional on-site nonlinearity.
method: Combines analytical and phase-space analysis to study the tunneling dynamics.
result: Shows that beyond a critical coupling strength, anomalous tunneling behavior emerges.
conclusion: The work provides a general theory for nonlinear LZ tunneling with sign-reversible coupling.

title: Equilibrium And Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions In Dipolar Atomic Josephson Junctions
authors: Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, And Luca Salasnich

An atomic Josephson junction realized with dipolar bosons in a double-well potential can be described by an extended Bose-Hubbard model in which dipolar interactions generate an effective on-site interaction and nearest-neighbor pair tunneling. Using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibrium and dynamical quantum phase transitions in dipolar atomic Josephson junctions using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
motivation: To understand the effects of dipolar interactions on quantum phase transitions and dynamics in a bosonic Josephson junction.
method: The authors use an extended Bose-Hubbard model with dipolar interactions, analyzed via mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
result: They identify equilibrium phase transitions and dynamical quantum phase transitions, characterized by changes in the order parameter and Loschmidt echo.
conclusion: Dipolar interactions lead to richer phase diagrams and dynamical behavior compared to standard Josephson junctions.

title: Application Of Quantum Annealing To Computation Of Molecular Properties
authors: Pradyot Pritam Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Pradyot Pritam Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present the results of our quantum annealing computations of the permanent electric dipole moments of several molecules. By applying an electric field as a perturbation and measuring the corresponding energy responses, the molecular electric dipole moments are obtained numerically through the fin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062808] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum annealing to compute molecular electric dipole moments.
motivation: To demonstrate the application of quantum annealing for computing molecular properties, specifically permanent electric dipole moments.
method: Quantum annealing is applied to molecular Hamiltonians; an electric field perturbation is used to extract dipole moments via finite-difference energy responses.
result: The computed dipole moments for several molecules are presented, showing agreement with known values.
conclusion: Quantum annealing can be a viable tool for computing molecular properties, though the approach is preliminary and limited to small molecules.

title: Optimally Driving Multiphoton Transitions In The Perturbative Single-mode Regime
authors: Frieder Lindel, Stefan Yoshi Buhmann, Andreas Buchleitner, And Edoardo G. Carnio
abstract:
Author(s): Frieder Lindel, Stefan Yoshi Buhmann, Andreas Buchleitner, and Edoardo G. Carnio

The rate of [MATH]-photon transitions in matter, induced by an incident light field, depends on the field's [MATH]-order coherence function. Consequently, the coherence properties of the light field may be shaped to increase the rate of multiphoton transitions. Here, we determine the optimal st…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063727] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes the coherence of a light field to maximize multiphoton transition rates in the perturbative single-mode regime.
motivation: Multiphoton transitions are important for spectroscopy and quantum control; shaping the coherence of light can enhance these transitions.
method: The authors derive optimal coherence functions for the light field using a perturbative approach and solve the optimization problem analytically.
result: They find that the optimal field is a coherent state for one-photon transitions, but for higher-order transitions, the optimal field has non-classical coherence properties.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for enhancing multiphoton processes by engineering the coherence of light, with potential applications in quantum optics and spectroscopy.

title: Stability Of Current-carrying States In Hard-core Bosons With Long-range Hopping On A Square Lattice
authors: Yoshihiro Yabuuchi And Ippei Danshita

We investigate the stability of current-carrying states with quasimomentum [MATH] in the Bose-condensed phase of the hard-core Bose-Hubbard model on a square lattice, where particles transfer between two sites separated by distance [MATH] with hopping amplitude decaying algebraically with [MATH] as $∝{r}^{−α…

tldr: This paper studies the stability of current-carrying states in hard-core bosons with long-range hopping on a square lattice, focusing on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the stability of superfluid currents in lattice models with long-range hopping is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamic aspects.
method: The authors use mean-field theory and numerical simulations to analyze the Bose-Hubbard model with algebraically decaying hopping amplitudes on a square lattice.
result: They find that current-carrying states become unstable above a critical current, and the stability depends on the hopping range and interaction strength.
conclusion: The work provides insights into superfluid transport in long-range interacting systems, but it is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Finite-size Effects On The Edge Loss Probability In non-Hermitian Quantum Walks

This behavior has been proven to arise from imaginary gap cl…

tldr: This paper studies finite-size effects on edge loss probability in non-Hermitian quantum walks, focusing on a dynamical bulk-edge relation.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of edge loss peaks in non-Hermitian quantum walks under finite-size conditions is important for practical implementations.
method: The authors analyze the dynamical bulk-edge relation analytically and numerically, examining how system size affects the power-law dependence and edge loss probability.
result: They find that finite-size effects modify the edge loss probability and the associated power-law scaling, with implications for the observability of the bulk-edge correspondence.
conclusion: Finite-size corrections must be accounted for when interpreting edge loss in non-Hermitian quantum walk experiments.

tldr: This paper analyzes tensor network loop cluster expansions as systematic corrections to belief propagation for quantum many-body problems.

title: Quantum Theory For Edge Current And Noise In Two-dimensional Topological Superconductors
authors: S. Pintus And A. Crépieux

result: The edge current is zero for nonchiral edge states and nonzero for chiral edge states, while edge noise is nonzero in both cases.

authors: Michael Kaicher, Joseph Vovrosh, Alexandre Dauphin, And Simon B. Jäger
abstract:

title: Propagation Of Short Pulses In Rydberg Exciton Medium Under Blockade Conditions
authors: Sylwia Zielińska-Raczyńska And David Ziemkiewicz
abstract:

tldr: This paper studies the propagation of short pulses in a Rydberg exciton medium under blockade conditions using density matrix formalism and FDTD method.
motivation: To understand the nonlinear optical effects and pulse propagation in Rydberg exciton systems, which are relevant for quantum optics and many-body physics.
method: The authors use density matrix formalism combined with the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method to simulate pulse propagation.

authors: Andoni Agirre, Thomas Frederiksen, Géza Giedke, And Tobias Graß

tldr: This paper uses matrix product states to identify and optimize spin models for Fermi-Hubbard ladders describing oligo(indenoindene) molecules, focusing on correlated magnetism in nanographenes.
motivation: To understand correlated magnetism in open-shell nanographenes by deriving accurate effective spin models from ab initio calculations.
method: Matrix product states (MPS) are used to solve the Fermi-Hubbard model for non-bipartite ladders and extract effective spin Hamiltonians.
result: The study identifies accurate spin models that capture the low-energy physics of the system, including magnetic ordering and gaps.
conclusion: The approach provides a systematic way to derive spin models for complex carbon-based materials, aiding in the design of molecular magnets.

motivation: Understanding localization phenomena in non-Hermitian systems is of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chain with period-2 mosaic modulation and nonreciprocal hopping, using numerical and possibly analytical methods to study localization transitions.

tldr: Benchmarks classical numerical methods for simulating the 2D transverse-field Ising model, comparing tensor networks, neural quantum states, and other techniques.
motivation: Understanding quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is challenging; this work aims to assess the performance of various classical simulation methods.
method: Applies a suite of numerical approaches including tensor networks, neural quantum states, and other large-scale classical methods to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model.
result: Provides a comparative analysis of accuracy and computational cost across methods for different parameter regimes.
conclusion: No single method universally outperforms others; the choice depends on the specific regime and desired accuracy.

tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced topological phases in a Chern insulator with strong magnetic disorder, demonstrating that directional disorder can create topological phases not present in clean systems.
motivation: To explore whether strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments can induce new topological phases in a Chern insulator, beyond what is possible in clean systems.
method: The authors use a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled to local magnetic moments with strong directional disorder, and analyze the resulting topological phases via numerical simulations.
result: They find that strong directional disorder gives rise to topological phases that are genuinely disorder-driven and cannot be realized in any clean system.
conclusion: Disorder can be a resource for engineering novel topological phases, expanding the possibilities for topological matter beyond clean systems.

tldr: This paper presents optimal parametric control strategies for DC transport across a Josephson junction using bichromatic and trichromatic driving.
motivation: To optimize the prefactor of the divergence of transport current in a parametrically driven Josephson junction.

result: They achieve optimized transport properties with improved prefactors for the current divergence.
conclusion: Parametric control can enhance DC transport in Josephson junctions, with potential applications in superconducting electronics.

authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan

result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage by outperforming classical methods in simulating the specific dynamics.
conclusion: The ultracold-atom processor provides a viable platform for demonstrating quantum advantage in practical simulations.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their analogy to quantum computation.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework by treating space and time on equal footing.
method: The review discusses discretized time evolution on lattice systems, brickwork quantum circuits, and the space-time duality mapping to simplify dynamics.
result: It provides a pedagogical overview of how space-time duality relates to exactly solvable models and quantum circuit dynamics.
conclusion: Space-time duality provides a powerful tool for understanding and computing quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum computation.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering their formation and quantum features.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic applications, and understanding their quantum properties may enable new functionalities.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including interactions and quantum tunneling.
result: It summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, such as quantum depinning and superposition states.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmionics is an emerging field with potential for future quantum technologies, but many open questions remain.

result: The Rydberg impurity spectroscopy can reveal signatures of BCS pairing and quasiparticle formation.
conclusion: Rydberg atoms can serve as local sensors for fermionic superfluids, offering a new tool for studying strongly correlated quantum matter.

motivation: To explore whether repulsive interactions can induce topological superconductivity in a Landau level, which is not possible for noninteracting electrons.

motivation: To achieve simultaneous lasing and absorption in a single photonic device, enabling multifunctional photonic applications.
method: The authors design a Fabry–Pérot microcavity with tailored gain and loss to support conjugate exceptional points, and use non-Hermitian topology to switch between lasing and absorption states.
result: The system exhibits frequency-matched dual-state coexistence of amplification and absorption.
conclusion: This work opens new opportunities for multifunctional photonic devices by exploiting non-Hermitian physics.

motivation: To achieve coherent control of the Goos-Hänchen shift, which is a spatial shift of reflected light, using a hybrid optomechanical system with excitons and molecular vibrations.

result: The Goos-Hänchen shift can be controlled by adjusting the pump field strength and the coupling parameters, showing tunable positive and negative shifts.

result: The analysis yields specific transition probabilities or entanglement dynamics for the system, though details are not provided in the abstract.

result: The analysis yields the dispersion relations and stability conditions for the altermagnetic BEC.
conclusion: Altermagnetism introduces new features in the BEC excitation spectrum, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063520] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.

title: Distinguishing Polarization Orientation Via Second-harmonic Generation In The Potential Sliding Ferroelectric ${\mathrm{SnP}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{6}$
authors: Fengfeng Ye, Qiankun Li, Zhuocheng Lu, Xinfeng Chen, Yang Li, Hua Wang, Lu You, And Gaoyang Gou

result: They demonstrate that SHG can effectively differentiate between opposite polarization orientations in SnP2S6.
conclusion: SHG is a reliable, non-destructive method for characterizing polarization in sliding ferroelectrics, aiding future device development.

title: Multiscale Study Of Various Topological Spin Textures In Two-dimensional Materials

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214446] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological spin textures in 2D magnetic materials using multiscale simulations, focusing on skyrmions and antiskyrmions.
motivation: To explore the diversity of topological spin textures in 2D materials beyond single-type textures, enabling potential applications in spintronics.
method: Uses first-principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations to model magnetic interactions and spin configurations in monolayer CrI3 and related materials.
result: Identifies conditions for stabilizing skyrmions, antiskyrmions, and bimerons, and maps their phase diagrams as functions of material parameters.
conclusion: 2D magnetic materials can host multiple topological spin textures, offering a platform for tunable spintronic devices.

authors: Huanpeng Bu, Han Ge, Fangli Li, Lei Xu, Jiayue Yuan, Tiantian Li, Junzhe Liu, Jian Chen, Ying Fu, Nan Zhao, Zhongwen Ouyang, Ping Miao, Jieming Sheng, And Liusuo Wu

motivation: To understand the thermodynamic properties and magnetic behavior of the layered Shastry-Sutherland magnet Eu2MgSi2O7, which features a quasi-two-dimensional orthogonal-dimer network of large-spin ions.
method: Comprehensive experimental study using thermodynamic measurements (e.g., specific heat, magnetization) under varying magnetic fields and temperatures, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: The paper maps out the entropy landscape and field-temperature phase diagram, revealing field-tuned thermodynamic transitions and magnetic ordering.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the low-temperature magnetism of large-spin Shastry-Sutherland systems, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics of computation, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Marginal Influence Of Anomalous Josephson Current On Odd-frequency Spin-triplet Pairing In Ferromagnetic Josephson Diodes
authors: Subhajit Pal And Colin Benjamin

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214516] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the influence of anomalous Josephson current on odd-frequency spin-triplet pairing in ferromagnetic Josephson diodes.
motivation: To understand the interplay between anomalous Josephson current and odd-frequency pairing in hybrid superconductor-ferromagnet junctions.
method: Theoretical analysis of two Josephson junction geometries with ferromagnetic layers, using Green's function techniques to compute pairing correlations.
result: The anomalous Josephson current has a marginal effect on odd-frequency spin-triplet pairing, with the pairing being robust against the anomalous current.
conclusion: Odd-frequency pairing in these junctions is largely unaffected by the anomalous Josephson current, indicating a decoupling between the two phenomena.

title: Anisotropic Vortex Motion And Two-dimensional Superconducting Transition
authors: Zhipeng Xu, Kun Jiang, And Jiangping Hu
abstract:

Vortex motion plays a central role in determining the resistance of two-dimensional superconductors, both in the context of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition and in the mixed state of type-II superconductors under magnetic fields. In this study, we introduce an anisotropic pinning…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214517] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic vortex motion and the BKT transition in two-dimensional superconductors, focusing on pinning effects and resistance.
motivation: Understanding vortex motion is crucial for determining resistance in 2D superconductors, especially in the context of BKT transitions and mixed states under magnetic fields.
method: The authors introduce an anisotropic pinning model and analyze its effect on vortex dynamics and the superconducting transition.
result: The study reveals how anisotropic pinning alters the BKT transition and the resistance in the mixed state.
conclusion: Anisotropic pinning significantly influences vortex motion and the superconducting transition, providing insights into 2D superconductor behavior.

title: Global Optimization Of Atomic Clusters Via Physically Constrained Tensor Train Decomposition
authors: Konstantin Sozykin, Nikita Rybin, Andrei Chertkov, Anh-Huy Phan, Ivan Oseledets, Alexander Shapeev, Ivan Novikov, And Gleb Ryzhakov

The global optimization of atomic clusters represents a fundamental challenge in computational chemistry and materials science due to the exponential growth of local minima with system size (i.e., the curse of dimensionality). We introduce a framework that overcomes this limitation by exploiting the…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224111] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.

motivation: Global optimization of atomic clusters is computationally challenging due to the exponential growth of local minima; existing methods often fail for larger systems.
method: The authors employ a tensor train (TT) decomposition to represent the potential energy surface, incorporating physical constraints (e.g., pairwise interactions) to reduce complexity, and use a global optimization algorithm on the TT format.
result: The method successfully identifies global minima for clusters up to 55 atoms, outperforming traditional approaches in efficiency and accuracy.
conclusion: Tensor train decomposition with physical constraints provides a scalable and effective framework for global optimization of atomic clusters, with potential applications in materials science.

title: Nonlinear Phononics In LaFeAsO: Optical Control Of The Crystal Structure Toward Possible Enhancement Of Superconductivity
authors: Shu Kamiyama, Tatsuya Kaneko, Kazuhiko Kuroki, And Masayuki Ochi

tldr: This paper uses nonlinear phononics to optically control the crystal structure of LaFeAsO to enhance superconductivity, but it is focused on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The goal is to tune the crystal structure of an iron-based superconductor toward an ideal configuration that maximizes superconductivity, using light-induced phonon excitation.
method: The authors simulate nonlinear phononics in LaFeAsO using first-principles calculations and model the structural response to coherent phonon excitation.
result: They find that specific phonon modes can induce a structural distortion that enhances the superconducting transition temperature.
conclusion: Nonlinear phononics offers a promising route to optically control superconductivity in iron-based superconductors, but the work is purely materials-oriented.

title: Multiband Superconductivity In The Kagome-lattice Superconductor ${\mathrm{Re}}_{2}\mathrm{Zr}$
authors: Gabriel Kuderowicz And Bartlomiej Wiendlocha
abstract:

tldr: A first-principles study of electronic structure, lattice dynamics, and superconductivity in the kagome-lattice compound Re2Zr, focusing on multiband superconductivity and electron-phonon coupling.
motivation: To understand the superconducting properties of Re2Zr, a kagome-lattice material that exhibits time-reversal symmetry breaking and unconventional pairing, using first-principles calculations.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) and density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) are used to compute electronic structure, phonon dispersion, and electron-phonon coupling, followed by solving the Eliashberg equations to estimate the superconducting transition temperature.
result: The calculations reveal multiband superconductivity with a superconducting gap structure involving multiple bands, and the electron-phonon coupling is sufficient to explain the observed Tc.
conclusion: Re2Zr is a conventional electron-phonon mediated superconductor despite its kagome lattice and unconventional pairing signatures, with multiband effects playing a key role.

tldr: This paper studies Berry-curvature-induced magnetotransport in nonmagnetic metals with inversion symmetry, focusing on bulk transport effects.
motivation: To understand how Berry curvature can influence electronic transport in nonmagnetic materials, which is typically associated with magnetic systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the Zeeman-activated Berry curvature contribution to magnetotransport in nonmagnetic metals with inversion symmetry.
result: They find that a Zeeman field can activate Berry-curvature-driven transport effects in the bulk of such materials.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of Berry curvature effects to nonmagnetic systems, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235138] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.

motivation: Understanding the allowed values of critical exponents is fundamental to renormalization-group theory of critical phenomena.
method: The authors propose a conjecture based on renormalization-group arguments and test it against known results.
result: They conjecture a lower bound for ν that should hold for a large class of continuous phase transitions.
conclusion: If true, the bound would constrain possible universality classes and guide future theoretical and numerical work.

result: Dielectric screening significantly modifies the Floquet band structure, affecting the observed sideband intensities.
conclusion: Screening must be accounted for in Floquet engineering of semiconductors for accurate band structure control.

result: The material exhibits a hedgehog-like spin texture with Weyl points in the 2D Brillouin zone, along with large spin splitting and nontrivial band topology.
conclusion: 2D chiral semiconductors can host Weyl-like spin textures, offering a platform for spintronic applications.

A distinctive feature of the approach is the use of complementary, readily generated training datasets spanning weak-, intermediate-, and strong-coupling regimes. method: A Transformer architecture is trained on complementary datasets covering weak to strong coupling, enabling system-size generalization.
result: The framework accurately captures the metal-to-insulator transition in the Hubbard model and generalizes from small to large systems.
conclusion: Transformer-based operator learning is a promising approach for modeling self-energies in strongly correlated materials.

method: The authors theoretically analyze electronic Raman scattering from spin-split bands in 2D metals with broken inversion symmetry, considering different types of spin-orbit coupling.
result: They find that the Raman response is sensitive to the spin texture and can distinguish between different spin-orbit coupling mechanisms.
conclusion: Electronic Raman scattering can be a useful probe of spin-orbit coupling and spin textures in 2D metals.

conclusion: The work provides a novel analytic tool for studying phase separation in 1D systems, with potential implications for non-relativistic holography.

method: High-dimensional bosonization technique is employed to derive an effective field theory for the transition.
