Chemical substitution offers an effective route to tune magnetic ordering and magnetocaloric performance in rare-earth (RE) oxides for cryogenic refrigeration. Here, we investigate the structural evolution, magnetic properties, and magnetocaloric effect of polycrystalline zircon-type ${}_…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214448] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chemical tuning of magnetic ordering and magnetocaloric effect in Gd1-xErxVO4 for cryogenic refrigeration.
motivation: To explore how chemical substitution in rare-earth oxides can optimize magnetic ordering and magnetocaloric performance for cryogenic cooling applications.
method: Polycrystalline samples of Gd1-xErxVO4 were synthesized and characterized by structural, magnetic, and heat capacity measurements to determine magnetic phase transitions and magnetocaloric effect.
result: Chemical substitution of Er for Gd tunes the magnetic ordering temperature and enhances the magnetocaloric response, with optimal performance at intermediate compositions.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that chemical substitution is an effective strategy to tailor magnetocaloric properties in zircon-type rare-earth vanadates for cryogenic refrigeration.

title: Anatomy Of The Modern Theory Of Orbital Magnetism From First Principles: Term-by-term Analysis In The Gauge-covariant Formalism
authors: Hojun Lee, Insu Baek, Mirco Sastges, Yuriy Mokrousov, Hyun-Woo Lee, And Dongwook Go
abstract:
Author(s): Hojun Lee, Insu Baek, Mirco Sastges, Yuriy Mokrousov, Hyun-Woo Lee, and Dongwook Go

We present an in-depth analysis of the orbital magnetism by means of the so-called modern theory based on the Berry phase across distinct classes of materials-[MATH] transition-metals, [MATH] metals, and transition metal dichalcogenides—highlighting the importance of the microscopic nature of band struct…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214449] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A first-principles analysis of orbital magnetism using Berry phase formalism across various materials.
motivation: To provide a detailed term-by-term understanding of orbital magnetization in different material classes.
method: Gauge-covariant formalism and Berry phase calculations applied to transition metals, metals, and transition metal dichalcogenides.
result: Identified contributions from different band structure features to orbital magnetization.
conclusion: The modern theory of orbital magnetism can be decomposed into physically interpretable terms, aiding material-specific predictions.

title: Structural And Magnetic Properties Of Epitaxially Strained (001)- And (111)-oriented ${\mathrm{Pb}}_{2}{\mathrm{CoTeO}}_{6}$ From First-principles
authors: Md Kamal Hossain And Elizabeth A. Nowadnick
abstract:
Author(s): Md Kamal Hossain and Elizabeth A. Nowadnick

The application of epitaxial strain to perovskite thin films has emerged as a powerful tool for tuning their properties, with differences observed between (001)- and (111)-oriented films. Although these effects have been extensively studied in [MATH] perovskites, the influence of strai…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224109] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of structural and magnetic properties of Pb2CoTeO6 under epitaxial strain.
motivation: To understand how epitaxial strain and film orientation affect the properties of double perovskite Pb2CoTeO6.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations for (001)- and (111)-oriented films under various strain conditions.
result: Strain and orientation significantly alter structural distortions and magnetic ordering, with potential for tuning multiferroic behavior.
conclusion: Epitaxial strain is an effective tool to control magnetic properties in this double perovskite, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Interplay Among Spin, Orbital, And Lattice Degrees Of Freedom In The Magnetocaloric Compound $\mathrm{Ho}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$
authors: Noriki Terada, Simon R. Larsen, Takafumi D. Yamamoto, Daisuke Okuyama, Hironori Nakao, Ginga Kitahara, Shuki Torii, Hiraku Saito, Taro Nakajima, Osamu Sakai, Hiroaki Mamiya, Kensei Terashima, Hiroyuki Takeya, Yoshihiko Takano, And Hideaki Kitazawa
abstract:
Author(s): Noriki Terada, Simon R. Larsen, Takafumi D. Yamamoto, Daisuke Okuyama, Hironori Nakao, Ginga Kitahara, Shuki Torii, Hiraku Saito, Taro Nakajima, Osamu Sakai, Hiroaki Mamiya, Kensei Terashima, Hiroyuki Takeya, Yoshihiko Takano, and Hideaki Kitazawa

We investigated the magnetic ordering, crystal lattice distortion, and spin dynamics in the magnetocaloric material [MATH] using neutron and x-ray diffraction (XRD), along with AC susceptibility measurements. Although [MATH] exhibits a ferromagnetic phas…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224436] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay of spin, orbital, and lattice degrees of freedom in the magnetocaloric compound HoB2 using neutron and x-ray diffraction and AC susceptibility.
motivation: To understand the magnetic ordering and crystal lattice distortion in HoB2, a magnetocaloric material, and to characterize its spin dynamics.
method: Neutron and x-ray diffraction (XRD) and AC susceptibility measurements were performed on HoB2.
result: The material exhibits a ferromagnetic phase with associated lattice distortions; detailed magnetic and structural parameters were determined.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetocaloric properties of HoB2 through its coupled spin-lattice behavior.

title: Magnetic Fluctuations And Anisotropy In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$: A Multi-orbital Study Based On $\mathrm{GGA}+U$ And Rpa
authors: Makoto Shimizu And Youichi Yanase
abstract:
Author(s): Makoto Shimizu and Youichi Yanase

Pressure-induced changes in the magnetic and superconducting properties of a spin-triplet superconductor candidate [MATH] have attracted considerable interest, underscoring the need for microscopic theoretical insight. In this paper, we investigate magnetic fluctuations and their aniso…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235137] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic fluctuations and anisotropy in UTe2 using GGA+U and RPA methods, focusing on pressure-induced changes in superconducting properties.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanism of spin-triplet superconductivity in UTe2 requires detailed knowledge of magnetic fluctuations and their anisotropy under pressure.
method: The authors employ first-principles GGA+U calculations combined with random phase approximation (RPA) to compute magnetic susceptibilities and fluctuation spectra.
result: They find that pressure modifies the magnetic fluctuation spectrum and anisotropy, which correlates with changes in superconducting pairing symmetry.
conclusion: The study provides theoretical insight into the pressure-dependent magnetic properties of UTe2, supporting the spin-triplet pairing scenario.

title: Dynamic Monte Carlo Study Of Rigidity Percolation Using An Event-based Ensemble Approach
authors: Mingzhong Lu, Yufeng Song, Qiyuan Shi, Ming Li, And Youjin Deng
abstract:
Author(s): Mingzhong Lu, Yufeng Song, Qiyuan Shi, Ming Li, and Youjin Deng

Rigidity percolation provides an important basis for understanding the onset of mechanical stability in disordered materials. While most studies on the triangular lattice have focused on static properties at fixed bond (site) occupation probabilities, the dynamics of the rigidity transition remain l…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064141] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies rigidity percolation dynamics on a triangular lattice using an event-based ensemble Monte Carlo method.
motivation: Understanding the onset of mechanical stability in disordered materials is important, but the dynamics of rigidity transitions have been less studied than static properties.
method: The authors employ an event-based ensemble approach to simulate the dynamic Monte Carlo process of rigidity percolation on a triangular lattice.
result: They characterize the dynamic rigidity transition and extract critical exponents.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamic aspects of rigidity percolation, but it is purely classical statistical mechanics with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Relations Among Different Inequality Measures In Complex Systems: From Kinetic Exchange To Earthquake Models
authors: Shohini Sen, Suchismita Banerjee, And Bikas K. Chakrabarti
abstract:
Author(s): Shohini Sen, Suchismita Banerjee, and Bikas K. Chakrabarti

We present a numerical study of several inequality measures across two kinetic wealth-exchange models with extreme inequality features (namely the Banerjee model, and the Chakraborti or yard-sale model) and two earthquake simulating models (namely the Chakrabarti-Stinchcombe two-fractal overlap mode…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064308] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies inequality measures in kinetic wealth-exchange and earthquake models, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand inequality distributions in complex systems such as economic models and earthquake simulations.
method: Numerical simulations of the Banerjee and Chakraborti wealth-exchange models and the Chakrabarti-Stinchcombe two-fractal overlap earthquake model.
result: Quantifies inequality measures like Gini coefficient and Kolkata index across these models.
conclusion: The models exhibit extreme inequality features, and the inequality measures show similar behavior across different complex systems.

title: Emergence Of A Fluctuation-driven Cooperative Solidlike Phase In Potts Model Monolayers
authors: Alexander J. Devanny And Laura J. Kaufman
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander J. Devanny and Laura J. Kaufman

Cellular Potts model (CPM) simulations display significant variation in dynamics, structural ordering, and observed phase transitions. Such differences may emerge, at least in part, because CPM simulations are not implemented in a uniform manner, specifically in terms of the definitions of cell peri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064410] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a fluctuation-driven cooperative solidlike phase in Potts model monolayers, focusing on cellular Potts model simulations and phase transitions.
motivation: To understand the variability in dynamics and phase transitions observed in cellular Potts model simulations due to different implementations.
method: The authors analyze the definitions of cell perimeter and area in the Potts model and perform simulations to study structural ordering and phase behavior.
result: They identify a fluctuation-driven cooperative solidlike phase that emerges under certain conditions.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of model implementation details and reveal a new phase in Potts model monolayers.

title: Discontinuous Wealth-gradient Transition Driving Cooperation
authors: Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, And Deok-Sun Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, and Deok-Sun Lee

The universal prevalence of cooperation is puzzling, as defection typically yields higher payoffs than cooperation, motivating searches for hidden pathways to cooperation. Here we study a game-theoretic model on a lattice structured population in which interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperation in a game-theoretic model on a lattice, focusing on wealth gradients and phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of cooperation despite the payoff advantage of defection is a classic puzzle in evolutionary game theory.
method: The authors analyze a spatial game where payoffs are scaled by the minimum wealth of interacting agents, using lattice simulations and analytical methods.
result: They find a discontinuous transition in cooperation levels driven by a wealth gradient, revealing a hidden pathway to cooperation.
conclusion: Wealth inequality can paradoxically promote cooperation under certain conditions, offering insights into social dynamics.

title: Spatial Correlations In Susceptible-infected-susceptible Processes On Random Regular Graphs
authors: Alexander Leibenzon, Samuel W. S. Johnson, Ruth E. Baker, And Michael Assaf
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Leibenzon, Samuel W. S. Johnson, Ruth E. Baker, and Michael Assaf

In network-based susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) models of infectious disease transmission, infection can only occur between directly connected individuals. This constraint naturally gives rise to spatial correlations between the states of neighboring nodes, as the infection status of connect…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064307] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spatial correlations in SIS epidemic models on random regular graphs using pair approximation and Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding how network structure and spatial correlations affect epidemic spread is important for predicting disease dynamics.
method: The authors derive a pair approximation model for the SIS process on random regular graphs and compare it with Monte Carlo simulations.
result: They find that pair approximation accurately captures the dynamics for large degree but fails for small degree due to strong correlations.
conclusion: Spatial correlations significantly impact the epidemic threshold and prevalence, especially in sparse networks.

title: ChronoCast: A Time-series Paradigm For Molecular Dynamics Simulation Using Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
authors: Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, And Jie Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, and Jie Chen

We propose a time-series paradigm named ChronoCast for molecular dynamics simulation using an advanced autoregressive Equivariant Graph Neural Network, which reformulates the conventionally time-consuming integration process into a forecasting task. This reformulation in turn offers a promising solu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065305] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: ChronoCast uses an equivariant graph neural network to forecast molecular dynamics trajectories, replacing traditional integration.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive due to numerical integration; a time-series forecasting approach can accelerate them.
method: An autoregressive equivariant graph neural network is trained to predict future atomic positions from past trajectory data.
result: The method achieves accurate long-term predictions with significant speedup over conventional MD integration.
conclusion: ChronoCast demonstrates that machine learning can effectively surrogate MD simulations, offering a new paradigm for computational chemistry.

title: Propagation Of Coherent Mechanical Waves In Stealth Hyperuniform Materials In The Transparent Regime
authors: Tony Valier-Brasier
abstract:
Author(s): Tony Valier-Brasier

Wave propagation in multiply scattering media is a fundamental and long-standing topic that has undergone renewed interest with the advent of metamaterials. In particular, disorder control is an efficient way to alter wave propagation. Stealth hyperuniform (SHU) media, characterized by the cancellat…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065505] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coherent mechanical wave propagation in stealth hyperuniform materials, focusing on the transparent regime.
motivation: Understanding wave propagation in disordered media is fundamental and relevant for metamaterial design.
method: Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of wave propagation in stealth hyperuniform elastic media.
result: Stealth hyperuniform materials exhibit a transparent regime for coherent mechanical waves due to suppressed long-range density fluctuations.
conclusion: Stealth hyperuniformity can be used to control wave propagation, with potential applications in acoustics and elasticity.

title: Algebraic To Exponential Decay Of Spatial Correlations In One-dimensional And Confined Hard-core Fluids: A Laplace-pole Analysis
authors: Ana M. Montero And Andrés Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Ana M. Montero and Andrés Santos

We derive the asymptotic behavior of the radial distribution function [MATH] for one-dimensional (1D) hard-rod systems and related quasi-one-dimensional geometries at high packing fractions using Laplace transform techniques and pole analysis. By identifying the poles and residues of the Laplace tra…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064133] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the asymptotic decay of spatial correlations in one-dimensional hard-rod fluids using Laplace transform pole analysis.
motivation: Understanding the decay of correlations in confined hard-core fluids is important for statistical mechanics of fluids and soft matter.
method: The authors use Laplace transform techniques and pole analysis to derive the asymptotic behavior of the radial distribution function at high packing fractions.
result: They show that spatial correlations decay algebraically in strictly 1D systems and exponentially in quasi-1D confined geometries.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting correlation decay in hard-core fluids, relevant to confined fluid systems.

title: Pacemaker-induced Spiral Wave Chimeras On A Sphere Of Delay-coupled Oscillators: Switching Between Different Spiral-phase Kinks
authors: Chol-Ung Choe, Ryong-Son Kim, And Jin-Song Kang
abstract:
Author(s): Chol-Ung Choe, Ryong-Son Kim, and Jin-Song Kang

Two-dimensional systems of nonlocally coupled oscillators exhibit spiral wave chimeras, a phenomenon that has garnered significant attention in nonlinear dynamics. These chimeras are characterized by the simultaneous presence of synchronized spiral regions and desynchronized phase-randomized cores. …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064206] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spiral wave chimeras in a system of delay-coupled oscillators on a sphere, focusing on switching between different spiral-phase kinks.
motivation: Spiral wave chimeras are a fascinating pattern in nonlinear dynamics, and understanding their behavior on curved surfaces like a sphere is of fundamental interest.
method: The authors use numerical simulations of a nonlocally coupled oscillator model on a sphere with time-delayed coupling, analyzing the emergence and switching of spiral-phase kinks.
result: They observe that pacemaker-induced spiral wave chimeras can switch between different spiral-phase kink configurations depending on parameters.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamics of chimera states on curved geometries, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Regime Identification And Control Of Extremes In The Nonautonomous Lorenz Model With Chaos And Intransitivity
authors: Moyan Liu, Qin Huang, And Upmanu Lall
abstract:
Author(s): Moyan Liu, Qin Huang, and Upmanu Lall

Adaptive chaos control has been studied extensively for autonomous systems. For real-world, nonautonomous systems, such as planetary weather, observations of the system state in response to seasonally and diurnally varying forcing are available only at discrete times and locations. We consider a sto…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064207] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies regime identification and control of extremes in a nonautonomous Lorenz model with chaos and intransitivity.
motivation: Real-world nonautonomous systems like planetary weather require adaptive chaos control, but existing methods focus on autonomous systems.
method: The authors consider a stochastic nonautonomous Lorenz model and develop a method for regime identification and control of extreme events.
result: The proposed approach successfully identifies regimes and controls extremes in the nonautonomous Lorenz model.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for adaptive control of extremes in nonautonomous chaotic systems, with potential applications in climate and weather.

title: General Approach For Partitioning And Phase Separation In Macromolecular Coexisting Phases
authors: Vikki Anand Varma And Alberto Scacchi
abstract:
Author(s): Vikki Anand Varma and Alberto Scacchi

Partitioning of (bio)materials in polymeric mixtures is a key phenomenon both in cellular environments, as well as in industrial applications. In cells, macromolecules are distributed among distinct biomolecular phases. The coexistence of polymeric aqueous phases in multicomponent systems has been w…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065414] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies partitioning and phase separation in macromolecular coexisting phases, a topic in soft matter physics.
motivation: Understanding how biomaterials partition among coexisting phases is important for cellular biology and industrial applications.
method: The authors develop a general theoretical approach based on polymer physics to describe partitioning in multicomponent polymeric mixtures.
result: They derive expressions for partition coefficients and phase diagrams for macromolecular systems.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for predicting partitioning behavior in complex polymer mixtures.

title: Resource And Population Dynamics In An Agent-environment Interaction Model
authors: Gaston Briozzo, Gustavo J. Sibona, And Fernando Peruani
abstract:
Author(s): Gaston Briozzo, Gustavo J. Sibona, and Fernando Peruani

In any ecosystem, the conditions of the environment and the characteristics of the species that inhabit it are entangled, coevolving in space and time. We introduce a model that couples active agents with a dynamic environment, interpreted as a nutrient source. Agents are persistent random walkers t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064406] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A model coupling active agents with a dynamic environment to study resource and population dynamics in ecosystems.
motivation: To understand the coevolution of species and their environment in ecosystems, where conditions and characteristics are entangled.
method: Introduces a model with persistent random walkers (agents) interacting with a dynamic nutrient source, analyzed via simulations.
result: The model reveals emergent population and resource patterns depending on agent mobility and environmental renewal.
conclusion: The coupling between agent behavior and environment dynamics is crucial for ecosystem stability and biodiversity.

title: Ligand-mediated Magnetic Coupling Across Metamagnetic Transitions In ${\mathrm{CrPS}}_{4}$
authors: Giuseppe Buccoliero, Rachel Nickel, Roberto Sant, Marli Dos Reis Cantarino, Andrei Rogalev, Nathan J. Yutronkie, Tristan Riccardi, Daniel A. Chaney, Kurt Kummer, Johann Coraux, And Nicholas B. Brookes
abstract:
Author(s): Giuseppe Buccoliero, Rachel Nickel, Roberto Sant, Marli dos Reis Cantarino, Andrei Rogalev, Nathan J. Yutronkie, Tristan Riccardi, Daniel A. Chaney, Kurt Kummer, Johann Coraux, and Nicholas B. Brookes

Chromium thiophosphate ([MATH]) is a long-known material: A layered semiconducting antiferromagnet. Its recently discovered gate-tunable metamagnetic phase transitions, the remarkable positive and oscillating magnetoresistance as a tunnel barrier, and its Fano-resonance luminescence, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023323] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates ligand-mediated magnetic coupling and metamagnetic transitions in CrPS4, a layered antiferromagnetic semiconductor.
motivation: To understand the microscopic origin of gate-tunable metamagnetic phase transitions and unusual magnetoresistance in CrPS4.
method: Combines X-ray absorption spectroscopy, X-ray magnetic circular dichroism, and density functional theory calculations to probe electronic and magnetic structure.
result: Identifies ligand-mediated superexchange as the dominant coupling mechanism and explains the metamagnetic transitions via competing exchange interactions.
conclusion: The findings provide a microscopic model for the magnetic properties of CrPS4, relevant for spintronic applications.

title: Contrasting Impurity-induced Magnetism And Dynamics In $2H\text{−}{\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Jonas A. Krieger, Igor P. Rusinov, Sourabh Barua, Aris Chatzichristos, Jared Croese, Derek Fujimoto, Stefan Holenstein, Victoria L. Karner, Ryan M. L. Mcfadden, John O. Ticknor, W. Andrew Macfarlane, Robert F. Kiefl, Geetha Balakrishnan, Evgueni V. Chulkov, Stuart S. P. Parkin, And Zaher Salman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas A. Krieger, Igor P. Rusinov, Sourabh Barua, Aris Chatzichristos, Jared Croese, Derek Fujimoto, Stefan Holenstein, Victoria L. Karner, Ryan M. L. McFadden, John O. Ticknor, W. Andrew MacFarlane, Robert F. Kiefl, Geetha Balakrishnan, Evgueni V. Chulkov, Stuart S. P. Parkin, and Zaher Salman

We investigate the behavior of interstitial [MATH] implanted near the surface of [MATH] using [MATH]-detected nuclear magnetic resonance. We find that, unlike the muon, [MATH] does not show any signature of induced magnetism. This result is consist…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023316] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies impurity-induced magnetism and dynamics in 2H-MoTe2 using β-NMR, finding no induced magnetism for Li8, contrasting with muon results.
motivation: To understand the behavior of interstitial impurities in transition metal dichalcogenides and resolve discrepancies between different probe particles.
method: β-detected nuclear magnetic resonance (β-NMR) was used to probe Li8 implanted near the surface of 2H-MoTe2, comparing with muon spin rotation results.
result: Li8 shows no signature of induced magnetism, unlike muons, indicating a strong dependence on the probe particle.
conclusion: The magnetic response of impurities in 2H-MoTe2 is highly sensitive to the specific probe, highlighting the need for careful interpretation of such measurements.

title: Machine-learning-guided Discovery Of Kagome Superconductors ${\mathrm{YRu}}_{3}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{LuRu}}_{3}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$
authors: Rose Albu Mustaf, Sajilesh K. P., Sanu Mishra, Junze Deng, Yi Jiang, Kaja H. Hiorth, Eeli O. Lamponen, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Päivi Törmä, Miguel A. L. Marques, B. Andrei Bernevig, And Emilia Morosan
abstract:
Author(s): Rose Albu Mustaf, Sajilesh K. P., Sanu Mishra, Junze Deng, Yi Jiang, Kaja H. Hiorth, Eeli O. Lamponen, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Päivi Törmä, Miguel A. L. Marques, B. Andrei Bernevig, and Emilia Morosan

We report the experimental discovery of bulk superconductivity in two kagome lattice compounds, [MATH] and [MATH], which were predicted through machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening combined with first-principles calculati…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023308] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Discovery of two new kagome superconductors via machine-learning-guided high-throughput screening and first-principles calculations.
motivation: To find new superconducting materials in the kagome lattice family, which are of interest for their exotic electronic properties.
method: Machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening combined with first-principles calculations to predict candidate compounds, followed by experimental synthesis and characterization.
result: Bulk superconductivity was discovered in YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2, confirming the predictions.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates the power of machine learning in discovering new superconductors, but the paper focuses on materials discovery rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Confinement And Finite-range Effects In A Quasi-two-dimensional Gas Of Fermionic Dimers
authors: Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, And Grigory E. Astrakharchik
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, and Grigory E. Astrakharchik

A study of a gas of fermionic dimers in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry induced by strong harmonic confinement in one direction is presented. Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo calculations are used to quantify the effects of confinement and finite interaction range on the equation of state and density profiles, with the results benchmarked against analytical theories.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022051] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A Monte Carlo study of fermionic dimers in a quasi-2D geometry, focusing on confinement and finite-range effects on the equation of state.
motivation: To understand how strong confinement and finite interaction range affect the properties of a gas of fermionic dimers, which is relevant to ultracold atomic physics.
method: Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the equation of state and density profiles, benchmarked against analytical theories.
result: Quantifies the effects of confinement and finite range, showing deviations from simple analytical models.
conclusion: The study provides benchmarks for future experiments and theoretical models of quasi-2D fermionic dimers.

title: Revealing Charge Anisotropies In Metal Compounds Via High-purity X-ray Polarimetry
authors: Lena Scherthan, Juliusz A. Wolny, Isabelle Faus, Olaf Leupold, Kai S. Schulze, Sebastian Höfer, Robert Loetzsch, Berit Marx-Glowna, Christopher E. Anson, Annie K. Powell, Ingo Uschmann, Hans-Christian Wille, Gerhard G. Paulus, Volker Schünemann, And Ralf Röhlsberger
abstract:
Author(s): Lena Scherthan, Juliusz A. Wolny, Isabelle Faus, Olaf Leupold, Kai S. Schulze, Sebastian Höfer, Robert Loetzsch, Berit Marx-Glowna, Christopher E. Anson, Annie K. Powell, Ingo Uschmann, Hans-Christian Wille, Gerhard G. Paulus, Volker Schünemann, and Ralf Röhlsberger

Linear polarization analysis of hard x-rays is employed to probe electronic anisotropies in metal-containing complexes with high selectivity. We use polarization-resolved nuclear forward scattering (PR-NFS) of synchrotron radiation at the 14.4 keV nuclear resonance of [MATH] to determine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023297] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses high-purity X-ray polarimetry to probe charge anisotropies in metal compounds via nuclear forward scattering.
motivation: Understanding electronic anisotropies in metal complexes is important for materials science and chemistry, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors employ polarization-resolved nuclear forward scattering (PR-NFS) of synchrotron radiation at the 14.4 keV nuclear resonance of 57Fe to measure linear polarization of hard X-rays.
result: The technique reveals charge anisotropies in metal-containing complexes with high selectivity.
conclusion: High-purity X-ray polarimetry is a powerful tool for probing electronic structure, but the work is purely in condensed matter characterization without quantum information or thermodynamics relevance.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature, characterized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but they are often fragile and only appear at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a material platform with intrinsic flat bands stable at room temperature.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and perform angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to map the electronic band structure, revealing flat bands that are robust to temperature.
result: They observe orbital-selective flat bands that persist up to room temperature, providing a tunable platform for studying strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: These materials offer a promising system for investigating flat-band physics and potentially realizing correlated phases without extreme cooling.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, and Liuyan Zhao

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
