Author(s): Kang-Ju Lee, Ki-Ahm Lee, Woong Kook, and Taehun Lee

Degree centrality is one of the most fundamental measures of local importance in directed networks. Its fractional version is defined via the fractional directed Laplacian with parameter [MATH], a well-known nonlocal operator. When [MATH], the fractional centrality reduces to the out-degree centrality. …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064310] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a fractional version of degree centrality for directed networks using the fractional directed Laplacian.
motivation: Degree centrality is a fundamental measure in network analysis, but its fractional generalization may capture nonlocal properties of directed networks.
method: The authors define fractional degree centrality via the fractional directed Laplacian with a parameter α, and analyze its properties.
result: They show that when α=1, the fractional centrality reduces to out-degree centrality, and they derive bounds and relationships with other centrality measures.
conclusion: Fractional degree centrality provides a new tool for analyzing directed networks, with potential applications in network science.

title: Atomic-scale Insights Into Melting And Supercooling Mechanism Of Sodium Acetate Trihydrate Via Molecular Dynamics
authors: Ping Li, Chuanshuai Dong, And Lizhi Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ping Li, Chuanshuai Dong, and Lizhi Zhang

Sodium acetate trihydrate (SAT) is a promising phase change material for thermal energy storage through phase transition, yet its microscopic mechanisms of phase transition, especially melting and intrinsic supercooling, remain unclear. In this study, all-atom molecular-dynamics simulations were per…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065419] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Molecular dynamics study of melting and supercooling in sodium acetate trihydrate for thermal energy storage.
motivation: To understand the microscopic mechanisms of phase transition in a phase change material for thermal energy storage.
method: All-atom molecular dynamics simulations of sodium acetate trihydrate.
result: Insights into melting and supercooling mechanisms at the atomic scale.
conclusion: The study provides atomic-scale understanding that could help improve thermal energy storage materials.

title: Second-order Modified Mean-field Theory For Textured Immobilized Magnetic Nanoparticles
authors: Elena V. Grokhotova, Jing Zhong, Alexey O. Ivanov, And Ekaterina A. Elfimova
abstract:
Author(s): Elena V. Grokhotova, Jing Zhong, Alexey O. Ivanov, and Ekaterina A. Elfimova

A second-order modified mean-field theory has been developed to predict the static magnetization and initial magnetic susceptibility of textured ensembles of immobilized interacting superparamagnetic nanoparticles with uniaxial anisotropy. The theory takes into account the orientational texture of t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065420] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops a second-order modified mean-field theory for magnetization of textured immobilized magnetic nanoparticles.
motivation: To accurately predict static magnetization and initial magnetic susceptibility of textured ensembles of immobilized superparamagnetic nanoparticles with uniaxial anisotropy.
method: Extends the modified mean-field theory to second order, incorporating orientational texture and interparticle interactions.
result: The theory provides improved predictions for magnetization curves and susceptibility compared to first-order theories.
conclusion: The second-order modified mean-field theory is a useful tool for describing magnetic properties of textured nanoparticle systems.

title: Topological Enhancement Of Protein Kinetic Stability
authors: João N. C. Especial And Patrícia F. N. Faísca
abstract:
Author(s): João N. C. Especial and Patrícia F. N. Faísca

Knotted proteins embed a physical (i.e., open) knot within their native structures. For decades, significant effort has been devoted to elucidating the functional role of knots in proteins, yet no consensus has been reached. Here, using extensive Monte Carlo off-lattice simulations of a simple struc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062402] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how topological knots in proteins enhance their kinetic stability using Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding the functional role of knots in proteins has been a long-standing question; this work aims to link knot topology to protein stability.
method: Extensive Monte Carlo off-lattice simulations of a simple structure-based model are used to compare folding kinetics of knotted and unknotted proteins.
result: The presence of a knot significantly increases the kinetic stability of the protein, making it more resistant to unfolding.
conclusion: Topological knots can serve as a mechanism to enhance protein kinetic stability, potentially explaining their evolutionary conservation.

title: Characterizing Emergent Multiscale Dynamics In Colloidal Nanoparticle Gels
authors: William D. Brackett, Zachary M. Sherman, Felix Lehmkühler, Thomas M. Truskett, And Delia J. Milliron
abstract:
Author(s): William D. Brackett, Zachary M. Sherman, Felix Lehmkühler, Thomas M. Truskett, and Delia J. Milliron

Characterizing the dynamics of nanoparticle gel networks demands a spatiotemporal resolution that no single technique can provide. This Perspective describes the opportunities to address this challenge using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy at fourth-generation light sources combined with complementary experimental and simulation tools. This should move the field beyond descriptive fundamental studies toward mechanistic understanding and design of nanoparticle gels with adaptive and programmable behaviors.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 061001] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This perspective discusses using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy at fourth-generation light sources to study multiscale dynamics in colloidal nanoparticle gels.
motivation: Characterizing the dynamics of nanoparticle gel networks requires spatiotemporal resolution beyond any single technique, motivating a combined experimental and simulation approach.
method: The paper proposes using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy at advanced light sources, complemented by other experimental and simulation tools, to probe dynamics across scales.
result: No new results are presented; the paper outlines opportunities for future mechanistic understanding and design of adaptive nanoparticle gels.
conclusion: The field can move from descriptive studies to mechanistic understanding and design of programmable nanoparticle gels using the proposed multiscale approach.

title: High-energy Pulsed Electron-beam-induced Phase Transitions In A Plasma-levitated Crystalline Dust Cluster
authors: Beatrice Paraschiv, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Adrian Scurtu, Maria L. Mitu, And Cătălin M. Ticoş
abstract:
Author(s): Beatrice Paraschiv, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Adrian Scurtu, Maria L. Mitu, and Cătălin M. Ticoş

Dust clusters with crystalline structure, formed by charged microparticles in complex plasmas, can undergo phase transitions under external influences. While many studies have focused on the effects of temperature and pressure on crystallization, it is worthwhile to investigate a different factor su…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065209] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase transitions in plasma-levitated crystalline dust clusters induced by high-energy pulsed electron beams.
motivation: To explore a new factor (electron beam irradiation) that can trigger phase transitions in dust clusters, beyond temperature and pressure.
method: Experimental: dust clusters are formed in a complex plasma and exposed to high-energy pulsed electron beams; structural changes are observed.
result: The electron beam induces phase transitions in the crystalline dust cluster, altering its structure.
conclusion: Electron beams can be used to control phase transitions in plasma crystals, offering a new tool for studying condensed matter in plasmas.

title: Force And Geometric Signatures Of The Creep-to-failure Transition In A Granular Pile
authors: Qing Hao, Luca Montoya, Elena Lee, Luke K. Davis, And Cacey Stevens Bester
abstract:
Author(s): Qing Hao, Luca Montoya, Elena Lee, Luke K. Davis, and Cacey Stevens Bester

This paper presents experiments on a quasi-two-dimensional pile of photoelastic disks and investigates the microscopic structural and dynamical changes underlying granular creep and the signatures of the creep-to-failure transition. The experiments report rearrangement, force, and geometric events before macroscopic grain motion at the surface is observed, indicating that subtle rearrangements in the force chain network precede macroscopic failure.

#ClearMotivation #ElegantVisuals


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065417] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies granular creep and failure in a photoelastic disk pile, focusing on force chain rearrangements before macroscopic failure.
motivation: To understand microscopic structural and dynamical changes underlying granular creep and the transition to failure.
method: Experiments on a quasi-2D pile of photoelastic disks, tracking rearrangement, force, and geometric events before macroscopic motion.
result: Subtle rearrangements in the force chain network precede macroscopic failure, providing signatures of the creep-to-failure transition.
conclusion: Force and geometric signatures can indicate imminent failure in granular materials.

title: Fast Local Motions And Their Transitions In Polybutadiene Across The Glass Transition
authors: Tatsuya Kikuchi, Ryo Mashita, Tomomi Masui, Toshiji Kanaya, Hiroyuki Kishimoto, And Kenji Nakajima
abstract:
Author(s): Tatsuya Kikuchi, Ryo Mashita, Tomomi Masui, Toshiji Kanaya, Hiroyuki Kishimoto, and Kenji Nakajima

We investigated the local dynamics of polybutadiene over a wide temperature range, from the glassy state to the liquid (rubbery) state, using quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS) combined in a recently developed modified mode distribution analysis. This approach enabled high-precision separation o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065418] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies local molecular motions in polybutadiene across the glass transition using neutron scattering.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of polymers near the glass transition is important for materials science.
method: Quasielastic neutron scattering combined with modified mode distribution analysis.
result: High-precision separation of different local motion modes and their temperature dependence.
conclusion: The local dynamics change character across the glass transition, providing insight into polymer relaxation.

title: When Surface Dynamics Fakes Symmetry: Oxygen On Rh(100) Revisited
authors: Lutz Hammer, Tilman Kißlinger, Margareta Wagner, Reinhard B. Neder, Michael Schmid, Ulrike Diebold, And M. Alexander Schneider
abstract:
Author(s): Lutz Hammer, Tilman Kißlinger, Margareta Wagner, Reinhard B. Neder, Michael Schmid, Ulrike Diebold, and M. Alexander Schneider

Heating a long-range ordered adsorbate phase beyond its stability temperature does not necessarily result in a disordered phase; it can also break up into heavily fluctuating ordered domains. Temporal and/or spatial averaging over these fluctuations may give the impression of both a wrong periodicit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023296] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oxygen adsorption on Rh(100) surface, revealing that fluctuating ordered domains can mimic a wrong surface periodicity.
motivation: To understand the behavior of adsorbate phases beyond their stability temperature and the effects of temporal/spatial averaging on observed surface structures.
method: Combined experimental techniques (STM, LEED) and theoretical modeling (DFT, Monte Carlo simulations) to analyze surface dynamics and domain fluctuations.
result: Heating the ordered phase leads to heavily fluctuating domains that, upon averaging, appear to have a different periodicity than the true ground state.
conclusion: Surface dynamics can fake symmetry, and care must be taken when interpreting averaged surface measurements.

title: Commissioning And Full Realization Of A Collinear Resonance Ionization Spectroscopy Setup At Beijing Radioactive Ion-beam Facility
authors: W. C. Mei et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): W. C. Mei et al.

A PLASEN (Precision LAser Spectroscopy for Exotic Nuclei) system, consisting of a compact radio-frequency quadrupole cooler buncher (RFQ-cb) and a collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup, has now been fully commissioned with radioactive ion beams at the Beijing Radioactive Ion-beam Facilit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023286] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Commissioning of a collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup for exotic nuclei at a radioactive ion-beam facility.
motivation: To enable precision laser spectroscopy of short-lived isotopes for nuclear structure studies.
method: A collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy system combined with a radio-frequency quadrupole cooler buncher was built and tested with radioactive ion beams.
result: The system was fully commissioned and demonstrated successful operation with radioactive beams.
conclusion: The setup is now operational for future nuclear physics experiments.

title: Circular Dichroism In The Photoelectron Angular Distribution Of Achiral Molecules
authors: Christian S. Kern, Xiaosheng Yang, Giovanni Zamborlini, Simone Mearini, Matteo Jugovac, Vitaliy Feyer, Umberto de Giovannini, Angel Rubio, Serguei Soubatch, Michael G. Ramsey, F. Stefan Tautz, And Peter Puschnig
abstract:
Author(s): Christian S. Kern, Xiaosheng Yang, Giovanni Zamborlini, Simone Mearini, Matteo Jugovac, Vitaliy Feyer, Umberto De Giovannini, Angel Rubio, Serguei Soubatch, Michael G. Ramsey, F. Stefan Tautz, and Peter Puschnig

Circular dichroism in the angular distribution (CDAD) is the effect that the angular intensity distribution of photoemitted electrons depends on the handedness of the incident circularly polarized light. The origin of CDAD can be manifold, including intrinsic properties of the system under study, su…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023275] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies circular dichroism in photoelectron angular distributions from achiral molecules, focusing on the role of molecular orientation and final-state scattering.
motivation: Understanding the origin of circular dichroism in photoemission from achiral molecules is important for interpreting experimental data and for potential applications in molecular imaging.
method: The authors combine experimental measurements of photoelectron angular distributions with theoretical simulations using multiple scattering and density functional theory.
result: They show that circular dichroism arises from the interplay between molecular orientation and final-state scattering effects, even in the absence of molecular chirality.
conclusion: The findings clarify the mechanisms behind CDAD in achiral systems and provide a framework for analyzing such effects in more complex molecules.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces 'super-resonance' to overcome the bandwidth limit of resonant modes and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Resonant modes typically have narrow bandwidths, limiting their application in broadband flow stabilization.
method: The authors propose a super-resonance mechanism that maintains a broadband out-of-phase response beyond conventional resonance bandwidth.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications.
conclusion: The concept of super-resonance breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, offering new possibilities for flow control.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits gravitational-wave detector sensitivity; understanding and reducing anisotropy could lower noise.
method: The authors use experimental techniques (e.g., Brillouin light scattering, ellipsometry) to characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica films.
result: They find hidden anisotropy that persists after standard heat treatment, indicating that current coating processes produce non-isotropic films.
conclusion: Coating design and postprocessing strategies must account for this anisotropy to reduce thermal noise in future detectors.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He
abstract:
Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in a superionic conductor using experimental techniques.
motivation: Understanding ion diffusion in superionic conductors is important for designing high-performance materials.
method: The authors use direct spatial and temporal characterization methods to track ion motion.
result: They provide detailed dynamics of ion diffusion in AgCrSe2.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of ion transport in superionic conductors.

title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi
abstract:
Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses using inelastic x-ray scattering, focusing on the effect of glass stability.
motivation: Understanding the relationship between glass stability and low-frequency vibrational modes is important for glass physics but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: Improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique was used to measure vibrational properties of vapor-deposited glasses with varying stability.
result: The technique clarifies connections between complex vibrations and glass properties, revealing how stability affects low-frequency modes.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of glass dynamics but are unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Subsurface Driven Size-Dependent Elasticity In Nanodiamond
authors: Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, And Chongxin Shan
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, and Chongxin Shan

Subsurface compliant regions in nanodiamond allow for an elastic response to strain, providing a method for engineering the mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021010] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies size-dependent elasticity in nanodiamond driven by subsurface compliant regions.
motivation: Understanding and engineering mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond is important for applications.
method: Experimental characterization and modeling of nanodiamond elasticity as a function of size.
result: Subsurface compliant regions enable elastic response to strain, leading to size-dependent elasticity.
conclusion: The findings provide a method for engineering mechanical properties of diamond at the nanoscale.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of the physics and chemistry of transplutonium elements under high pressure, focusing on their electronic properties and behavior in metals, alloys, and compounds.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear power and waste management, and their 5f electrons exhibit unique localized/itinerant behavior under pressure, motivating a comprehensive review.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium metals, alloys, compounds, and coordination complexes under high pressure, summarizing key findings from the literature.
result: The review highlights the complex electronic structure and phase transitions of transplutonium materials under pressure, including the interplay between localized and itinerant 5f electrons.
conclusion: The work expands understanding of transplutonium materials under extreme conditions, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger connections.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, and their detection could reveal physics of dense matter.
method: The paper surveys detection prospects with future detectors and discusses simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It outlines the potential for multimessenger observations to inform nuclear astrophysics and condensed matter physics.
conclusion: Multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves will deepen understanding of neutron star interiors.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the interdisciplinary nature of physics.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics as a field of study.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture.
result: No novel research results; a retrospective view.
conclusion: Physics is a way of thinking that transcends traditional boundaries.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This is the Nobel Lecture by Geoffrey Hinton on Boltzmann machines, a foundational concept in machine learning.
motivation: To present the historical development and significance of Boltzmann machines in the context of artificial neural networks and their impact on physics and machine learning.
method: The lecture reviews the conceptual framework of Boltzmann machines, including their energy-based model and learning algorithm.
result: Boltzmann machines are a class of stochastic neural networks that can learn complex probability distributions, influencing modern deep learning.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines represent a key intersection between statistical physics and machine learning, but the lecture does not present new research results.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete defect picture.
result: The review highlights capabilities and limitations of each technique and cases where combining them yields more comprehensive disorder characterization.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy techniques, especially when combined, provide valuable atomic-scale disorder information for semiconductor materials.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions in stars is crucial for stellar burning and element formation, but many reactions are difficult to measure directly.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects.
result: Provides an overview of the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory.
conclusion: New ideas for studying these reactions on Earth are described, but the paper is purely nuclear astrophysics.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and self-consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed using all relevant experimental and theoretical data up to the end of 2022, following established CODATA procedures.
result: A new set of recommended values and uncertainties for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided.
conclusion: The 2022 CODATA values supersede previous sets and serve as the internationally accepted reference for fundamental constants.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper reviews the theoretical background of Wannier functions and describes the interoperable software ecosystem, including codes for construction, post-processing, and applications.
result: The review highlights the widespread use of Wannier functions in areas such as topological invariants, transport, and spectroscopy, and the growing ecosystem of software tools.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for the electronic-structure community, enabling accurate and insightful materials simulations.

title: Kinetic Solitary Electrostatic Structures In Collisionless Plasma: Phase-space Holes
authors: I. H. Hutchinson
abstract:
Author(s): I. H. Hutchinson

Plasma is usually taught to be a quasineutral gas of charged and neutral particles that exhibits collective behavior. However, satellites regularly observe solitary potential structures in space plasmas that are isolated positive or negative potential humps, called electron or ion holes. In the 1970s, laboratory observations were made of electron holes. This review presents an overview of the observation of these electrostatic structures and presents their origin and their stability, using analytic theory and simulations. The role of kinetically unstable velocity distributions is identified as a key driver.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045007] Published Tue Dec 10, 2024.
tldr: A review of kinetic solitary electrostatic structures (phase-space holes) in collisionless plasma, covering observations, theory, and simulations.
motivation: To understand the origin, stability, and dynamics of isolated potential humps observed in space plasmas, which are not explained by standard fluid models.
method: Review of satellite observations, analytic theory, and particle-in-cell simulations of electron and ion holes.
result: Phase-space holes arise from kinetically unstable velocity distributions and can be stable over long times, playing a role in plasma turbulence and transport.
conclusion: Phase-space holes are ubiquitous in space plasmas and their kinetic nature is essential for understanding their formation and persistence.

title: Strings From Almost Nothing
authors: Clifford Cheung, Grant N. Remmen, Francesco Sciotti, And Michele Tarquini
abstract:
Author(s): Clifford Cheung, Grant N. Remmen, Francesco Sciotti, and Michele Tarquini

Using a “bootstrap” approach, researchers show that a small set of assumptions may naturally lead to a string-theory description of certain high-energy processes.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251601] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses a bootstrap approach to derive string-theory descriptions of high-energy processes from minimal assumptions.
motivation: To understand how string theory emerges from basic principles without assuming its full structure.
method: The authors apply a bootstrap method, imposing consistency conditions like unitarity and crossing symmetry to constrain scattering amplitudes.
result: They show that a small set of assumptions naturally leads to a string-theory description of certain high-energy processes.
conclusion: String theory may be more inevitable than previously thought, emerging from simple physical principles.

title: Standard Model Baryon Number Violation At Zero Temperature From Higgs Bubble Collisions
authors: Nabeen Bhusal, Simone Blasi, Martina Cataldi, Aleksandr Chatrchyan, Marco Gorghetto, And Géraldine Servant
abstract:
Author(s): Nabeen Bhusal, Simone Blasi, Martina Cataldi, Aleksandr Chatrchyan, Marco Gorghetto, and Géraldine Servant

We compute for the first time baryon number violation at zero temperature from Higgs bubble collisions and find that it can be of the same order as that from thermal sphalerons in the symmetric phase at electroweak temperatures. We study the dependence of the rate of Chern-Simons number transitions …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241803] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies baryon number violation from Higgs bubble collisions at zero temperature, a topic in high-energy physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: To understand baryogenesis and the origin of matter-antimatter asymmetry, specifically whether bubble collisions during a first-order electroweak phase transition can produce baryon number violation at zero temperature.
method: The authors compute the rate of Chern-Simons number transitions during Higgs bubble collisions using numerical simulations and analytical estimates.
result: They find that baryon number violation from bubble collisions can be comparable to that from thermal sphalerons in the symmetric phase at electroweak temperatures.
conclusion: Higgs bubble collisions provide a new source of baryon number violation that may be relevant for electroweak baryogenesis scenarios.

title: First Observation Of Deuteron-$\mathrm{Λ}$ Correlations At Rhic
authors: B. E. Aboona et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. E. Aboona et al. (STAR Collaboration)

Precise experimental information on hyperon-nucleon interactions is scarce but of paramount importance to our understanding of the inner structure of compact stars. In this Letter, we report the first experimental results of correlation functions between deuterons ([MATH]) and [MATH] hyperons in …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 242303] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: First experimental observation of deuteron-Λ correlations at RHIC, providing insights into hyperon-nucleon interactions relevant to compact star structure.
motivation: Hyperon-nucleon interactions are poorly understood but crucial for modeling the inner structure of compact stars like neutron stars.
method: Measured correlation functions between deuterons and Λ hyperons in high-energy heavy-ion collisions at RHIC using the STAR detector.
result: Reported the first experimental correlation functions for deuteron-Λ pairs, revealing attractive interactions.
conclusion: The results provide new constraints on hyperon-nucleon interactions, improving our understanding of dense nuclear matter.

title: Periodic Fracture Of Active Tissues
authors: Yue Qian, Yue Li, And Bo Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Qian, Yue Li, and Bo Li

Fracture typically signifies mechanical failure in engineering materials, whereas controlled cracking may actively sculpt tissues through precise biological regulation. Here, we establish a multiscale nonlinear peridynamic theory that accounts for cellular mechanosensing to decipher the spontaneous …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 248402] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a multiscale peridynamic theory for periodic fracture in active biological tissues, driven by cellular mechanosensing.
motivation: Understanding how controlled cracking sculpts tissues during morphogenesis, as opposed to being a sign of mechanical failure.
method: A multiscale nonlinear peridynamic model incorporating cellular mechanosensing and active forces.
result: The model predicts spontaneous periodic fracture patterns that match experimental observations in developing tissues.
conclusion: Active fracture can be a regulated morphogenetic mechanism, with implications for tissue engineering and developmental biology.

title: Properties Of Heavy Cosmic Nuclei Phosphorus, Chlorine, Argon, Potassium, And Calcium: Results From The Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer
authors: A. Aceituno et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. Aceituno et al. (AMS Collaboration)

We report the unique properties of cosmic phosphorus (P), chlorine (Cl), argon (Ar), potassium (K), and calcium (Ca) fluxes in the GV to TV rigidity range collected by the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS) on the International Space Station. With a total of one million events collected over 13.5 yea…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241002] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports measurements of cosmic ray fluxes for heavy nuclei (P, Cl, Ar, K, Ca) from the AMS experiment.
motivation: To understand the properties and origins of heavy cosmic nuclei in the Galaxy.
method: Data collected by the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer on the ISS over 13.5 years, with about one million events analyzed in the GV to TV rigidity range.
result: Unique properties of the fluxes of phosphorus, chlorine, argon, potassium, and calcium are presented.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into cosmic ray propagation and nucleosynthesis.

title: Probing Scalar-Neutrino And Scalar-Dark-Matter Interactions With PandaX-4T
authors: Tao Li et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Li et al. (PandaX Collaboration)

Scalar-mediated interactions may exist among neutrinos, dark matter particles, or between the two. Double [MATH]-decay experiments provide a powerful tool to probe such exotic interactions. Using [MATH] double [MATH]-decay data from PandaX-4T, we perform the first direct spectral search in th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241802] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses PandaX-4T double beta decay data to search for scalar-mediated interactions between neutrinos and dark matter.
motivation: To probe exotic scalar-mediated interactions among neutrinos and dark matter particles using direct detection experiments.
method: Spectral analysis of double beta decay data from the PandaX-4T experiment to constrain scalar coupling parameters.
result: First direct spectral search for scalar-neutrino and scalar-dark-matter interactions, setting new limits on coupling strengths.
conclusion: The PandaX-4T data provide competitive constraints on scalar-mediated interactions, but no evidence for new physics is found.

title: Leading Effective Field Theory Corrections To The Kerr Metric At All Spins
authors: Pedro G. S. Fernandes
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro G. S. Fernandes

The leading corrections to general relativity can be parametrized by higher-derivative interactions in a low-energy effective field theory, in a way that is general and agnostic to the precise UV completion of gravity. Using numerical methods, we compute the leading-order corrections to the Kerr met…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241401] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes leading effective field theory corrections to the Kerr metric for all spins using numerical methods.
motivation: To parametrize and compute corrections to general relativity from higher-derivative interactions in a low-energy effective field theory, agnostic to UV completion.
method: Numerical methods are used to solve the modified field equations and compute corrections to the Kerr metric.
result: The leading-order corrections to the Kerr metric are obtained for all spins.
conclusion: The results provide a general parametrization of deviations from general relativity in black hole spacetimes.

title: Observation Of The Radiative Decay ${D}_{s0}^{*}(2317{)}^{+}→{D}_{s}^{*+}γ$
authors: M. Abumusabh et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Abumusabh et al. (Belle and Belle II Collaboration)

An exotic meson’s photon-emitting decay opens a window into the particle’s long-debated structure.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241901] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Observation of the radiative decay of an exotic meson, D_s0*(2317)+ → D_s*+ γ, providing insight into its internal structure.
motivation: The D_s0*(2317)+ meson has a debated structure; its radiative decay can reveal its composition.
method: Analysis of data from Belle and Belle II experiments to measure the decay branching fraction.
result: First observation of the radiative decay with a measured branching fraction.
conclusion: The decay rate supports certain theoretical models of the meson's structure.

title: Laser-Plasma Based Seeded Free Electron Laser In The High-Gain Regime
authors: Marie Labat, Susanne Schöbel, Amin Ghaith, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Maxwell Laberge, Eléonore Roussel, Ulrich Schramm, Patrick Ufer, Marie-Emmanuelle Couprie, And Arie Irman
abstract:
Author(s): Marie Labat, Susanne Schöbel, Amin Ghaith, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Maxwell LaBerge, Eléonore Roussel, Ulrich Schramm, Patrick Ufer, Marie-Emmanuelle Couprie, and Arie Irman

The realization of compact laser-plasma accelerator (LPA) driven free electron lasers (FELs) has been attempted for nearly two decades, yet, difficult to overcome electron beam quality and stability issues prevented FEL lasing until recently. LPA based FEL is now demonstrated in both the self-amplif…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 245001] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a laser-plasma accelerator driven free electron laser in the high-gain regime, a milestone in compact FEL technology.
motivation: To realize compact free electron lasers driven by laser-plasma accelerators, overcoming long-standing beam quality and stability issues.
method: Experimental demonstration of seeded FEL operation using a laser-plasma accelerator, achieving high-gain amplification.
result: Successful lasing in the high-gain regime, validating the LPA-based FEL concept.
conclusion: Laser-plasma accelerator driven FELs are now feasible, paving the way for compact, high-brightness X-ray sources.

title: Ablating Pellets For Areal Density Symmetry Control In Indirectly Driven Inertial Confinement Fusion Target Designs
authors: O. A. Hurricane, D. J. Strozzi, S. A. Maclaren, And C. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): O. A. Hurricane, D. J. Strozzi, S. A. Maclaren, and C. Weber

Asymmetry of the compressed fusion fuel configuration, as characterized by a variation in areal density, in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) implosions is a known performance limitation. While ignition has been achieved on the National Ignition Facility (NIF), implosion symmetry was not perfect, an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 245101] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to control areal density symmetry in inertial confinement fusion using ablating pellets.
motivation: Asymmetry in compressed fusion fuel limits performance in ICF implosions; controlling areal density symmetry is crucial for achieving ignition.
method: The authors propose using ablating pellets to adjust the areal density distribution in indirectly driven target designs, likely through simulations or experiments.
result: The technique demonstrates improved symmetry control, potentially enhancing fusion performance.
conclusion: Ablating pellets offer a viable approach to mitigate asymmetry in ICF, advancing toward more robust ignition.

title: Topological Friction: Insight From Dynamics Of A Test Chain In A Fixed-Topology Polymer Network
authors: Zhenhua Wang, Yuyuan Lu, Lijia An, And Zhen-Gang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhua Wang, Yuyuan Lu, Lijia An, and Zhen-Gang Wang

The tube model has long served as a cornerstone of entangled polymer dynamics and rheology. We test some of the key concepts of the tube model by investigating the equilibrium dynamics of a free chain in a fixed-topology polymer network using molecular dynamics simulation. Our results reveal signifi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 248101] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of a free chain in a fixed-topology polymer network using molecular dynamics, challenging the tube model of entangled polymer dynamics.
motivation: To test key concepts of the tube model, which is a cornerstone of entangled polymer dynamics and rheology.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of a free chain in a fixed-topology polymer network.
result: The results reveal significant deviations from the predictions of the tube model.
conclusion: The tube model may need revision to account for topological friction in polymer networks.

title: Tangential Forces Govern The Viscous-Inertial Transition In Dense Frictional Suspensions
authors: Sudarshan Konidena, Franco Tapia, Alireza Khodabakhshi, Élisabeth Guazzelli, Pascale Aussillous, And Bernhard Vowinckel
abstract:
Author(s): Sudarshan Konidena, Franco Tapia, Alireza Khodabakhshi, Élisabeth Guazzelli, Pascale Aussillous, and Bernhard Vowinckel

We present particle-resolved simulations of dense frictional suspensions undergoing the viscous-inertial transition using pressure-imposed rheology. By varying the fluid viscosity, shear rate, and granular pressure, we demonstrate that the transition occurs at a Stokes number of [MATH] (close to the v…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 248201] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the viscous-inertial transition in dense frictional suspensions using particle-resolved simulations, focusing on tangential forces.
motivation: Understanding the transition from viscous to inertial regimes in dense suspensions is important for industrial and natural processes, but the role of tangential forces was previously unclear.
method: Particle-resolved simulations with pressure-imposed rheology were performed, varying fluid viscosity, shear rate, and granular pressure to isolate the effect of tangential forces.
result: The transition occurs at a Stokes number close to the viscous-inertial crossover, and tangential forces are found to govern the transition.
conclusion: Tangential forces are key to the viscous-inertial transition in dense frictional suspensions, providing a mechanistic explanation for the observed rheological behavior.

title: Stark Effect In Molecular Rydberg States: Calculation Of Rydberg-Stark Manifolds Of ${\mathrm{H}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}$ Including Fine And Hyperfine Structures
authors: I. Doran, L. Jeckel, M. Beyer, Ch. Jungen, And F. Merkt

Author(s): I. Doran, L. Jeckel, M. Beyer, Ch. Jungen, and F. Merkt

We present a general theoretical treatment and calculations of the fine and hyperfine structures in the spectra of high-[MATH] molecular Rydberg states in static uniform electric fields. The treatment combines (i) multichannel quantum-defect theory and long-range polarization models to determine the fi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062812] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a theoretical treatment and calculations of fine and hyperfine structures in molecular Rydberg states under static electric fields.
motivation: Understanding Stark effects in molecular Rydberg states is important for spectroscopy and molecular physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors combine multichannel quantum-defect theory with long-range polarization models to compute Stark manifolds including fine and hyperfine structures for H2 and D2.
result: They provide detailed calculations of energy levels and transition probabilities for high-n Rydberg states in electric fields.
conclusion: The work advances molecular spectroscopy but has no relevance to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Effects Of Electric Field Rising Time On Polarization Switching In Ferroelectrics
authors: Bowen Li, Jinhong Li, Wenpeng Zhu, Haohua Wen, And Yue Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Bowen Li, Jinhong Li, Wenpeng Zhu, Haohua Wen, and Yue Zheng

The electric field rising time [MATH] is frequently overlooked in ultrafast ferroelectric switching studies, despite its critical role in switching dynamics and mechanism discrimination. Using stochastic phase-field simulations of [MATH], we systematically investigate [MATH] effe…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224112] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of electric field rising time on polarization switching in ferroelectrics using stochastic phase-field simulations.
motivation: The electric field rising time is often overlooked in ultrafast ferroelectric switching studies, yet it critically influences switching dynamics and mechanism discrimination.
method: Stochastic phase-field simulations are used to systematically investigate the effects of rising time on polarization switching.
result: The rising time significantly affects switching behavior and can alter the dominant switching mechanism.
conclusion: Rising time must be considered in ultrafast ferroelectric switching experiments to correctly interpret dynamics.

title: From Spark To Conflagration: A Multiscale Thermodynamic-percolation Framework For Wildland-fire Spread
authors: Xiaoping Shi, Mir Faizal, Arshid Shabir, And Behnam Pourhassan
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoping Shi, Mir Faizal, Arshid Shabir, and Behnam Pourhassan

Wildland fire operates across multiple spatial and temporal scales, linking local combustion chemistry and turbulent heat transport to continental patterns of burned area. A quantitative bridge between microscale ignition physics and macroscale propagation has remained elusive because operational si…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064143] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a multiscale thermodynamic-percolation framework for wildland-fire spread, bridging microscale ignition to macroscale propagation.
motivation: A quantitative bridge between microscale ignition physics and macroscale propagation has been elusive in operational fire models.
method: The authors combine thermodynamic principles with percolation theory across multiple spatial and temporal scales.
result: The framework successfully links local combustion and heat transport to large-scale burned area patterns.
conclusion: The model provides a new multiscale approach to understanding and predicting wildland-fire spread.

title: Evolution Of Localized Pulses In The Defocusing Modified Korteweg–de Vries Equation Theory
authors: L. F. Calazans de Brito, A. Gammal, And A. M. Kamchatnov
abstract:
Author(s): L. F. Calazans de Brito, A. Gammal, and A. M. Kamchatnov

In this work, we develop, in the Gurevich-Pitaevskii framework, an analytic theory for the evolution of localized pulses in the defocusing modified Korteweg–de Vries equation theory for situations when a dispersive shock does not eventually transform into a sequence of well-separated solitons. We fo…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064208] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytic theory for localized pulse evolution in the defocusing modified Korteweg–de Vries equation using the Gurevich-Pitaevskii framework.
motivation: To understand the evolution of localized pulses in nonlinear wave systems where dispersive shocks do not break into solitons.
method: Analytic theory based on the Gurevich-Pitaevskii approach, applied to the defocusing modified Korteweg–de Vries equation.
result: Provides a description of pulse evolution and wave breaking in this specific nonlinear system.
conclusion: The theory successfully models pulse dynamics in regimes where soliton formation is suppressed.

title: Effect Of Temporary Lockdowns On Disease Extinction Risk In Assortative Networks
authors: Elad Korngut And Michael Assaf
abstract:
Author(s): Elad Korngut and Michael Assaf

Changing environmental conditions can significantly affect the dynamics of disease spread. These changes may arise naturally or result from human interventions; in the latter case, lockdown measures that lead to abrupt but temporary reductions in transmission rates are used to combat disease spread.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064309] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of temporary lockdowns on disease extinction in assortative networks using stochastic modeling.
motivation: Understanding how temporary lockdowns affect disease extinction risk is crucial for public health policy, especially in structured populations.
method: The authors develop a stochastic model of disease spread on assortative networks and analyze the probability of extinction under temporary lockdown scenarios.
result: They find that temporary lockdowns can significantly increase extinction probability, with the effect depending on network assortativity and lockdown timing.
conclusion: Temporary lockdowns are effective in reducing disease extinction risk, but their impact is modulated by network structure and intervention timing.

title: Dynamic Stabilization Of The Isolated Internal Defect In The Presence Of A Temporally Modulated Laser Prepulse
authors: Y. Z. Han, K. G. Zhao, Z. Y. Li, Y. X. Liu, C. Xue, J. W. Li, Z. Chen, J. Q. Dong, J. F. Wu, L. F. Wang, And W. Y. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Z. Han, K. G. Zhao, Z. Y. Li, Y. X. Liu, C. Xue, J. W. Li, Z. Chen, J. Q. Dong, J. F. Wu, L. F. Wang, and W. Y. Zhang

Hydrodynamic instabilities seeded by isolated internal defects remain a critical performance-limiting factor in inertial confinement fusion experiments. Here we extend the concept of dynamic stabilization via temporally modulated laser pulses from the main drive [K. G. Zhao et al.,
tldr: This paper studies dynamic stabilization of hydrodynamic instabilities seeded by internal defects in inertial confinement fusion using temporally modulated laser prepulses.
motivation: Hydrodynamic instabilities from isolated internal defects limit performance in inertial confinement fusion experiments.
method: The authors extend the concept of dynamic stabilization via temporally modulated laser pulses from the main drive to the prepulse regime.
result: The modulated prepulse can stabilize the defect-induced instability.
conclusion: Dynamic stabilization with modulated prepulses may improve fusion target performance.

title: Self-propelled Droplet Dynamics On Superhydrophobic Surfaces Under Low-pressure Conditions
authors: Xiaonan Li, Jiayi Zhou, Haiyan Luo, Xueli Zheng, And Guo Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaonan Li, Jiayi Zhou, Haiyan Luo, Xueli Zheng, and Guo Chen

The self-removal of sessile droplets under low-pressure conditions is critical for extreme-environment surface engineering. Combining high-speed photography with quantitative analysis, we reveal the unique dynamics of ethylene glycol-water solution droplets on irregular micro-nanostructured superhyd…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065506] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of self-propelled droplets on superhydrophobic surfaces under low pressure, focusing on fluid mechanics and surface engineering.
motivation: Understanding droplet self-removal under low pressure is important for extreme-environment surface engineering applications.
method: High-speed photography and quantitative analysis are used to observe ethylene glycol-water solution droplets on irregular micro-nanostructured superhydrophobic surfaces.
result: The paper reveals unique dynamics of droplet motion under low-pressure conditions.
conclusion: The findings contribute to surface engineering for extreme environments but have no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Plume Stretching In The Trapped Region Of A Reoriented Potential Mixer
authors: Roseanna M. Neupauer, James D. Meiss, And Tomás G. Dabove
abstract:
Author(s): Roseanna M. Neupauer, James D. Meiss, and Tomás G. Dabove

The reoriented potential mixer (RPM) can enhance mixing and reaction during in situ remediation of contaminated groundwater, in which a chemical or biological amendment is introduced into a contaminant plume to react with and degrade the contaminant. Each step of the RPM consists of dipole flow betw…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065108] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fluid mixing in a reoriented potential mixer for groundwater remediation, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Enhance in situ remediation of contaminated groundwater by improving mixing and reaction between an introduced amendment and a contaminant plume.
method: Analyzes plume stretching in the trapped region of a reoriented potential mixer using dipole flow and reorientation steps.
result: Characterizes the stretching dynamics and mixing efficiency in the trapped region.
conclusion: The reoriented potential mixer can improve mixing, but the paper is purely classical fluid dynamics.

title: Bifurcations And Multistability In Inducible Three-gene Toggle Switch Networks
authors: Rebecca J. Rousseau And Rob Phillips
abstract:
Author(s): Rebecca J. Rousseau and Rob Phillips

Control of transcription presides over a vast array of biological processes, including those mediated by gene regulatory circuits that exhibit multistability. Within these circuits, two- and three-gene network motifs are particularly critical to the repertoire of metabolic and developmental pathways…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064408] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bifurcations and multistability in a synthetic three-gene toggle switch network, a topic in systems biology.
motivation: Understanding multistability in gene regulatory circuits is important for biological processes and synthetic biology.
method: The authors analyze a mathematical model of a three-gene toggle switch using bifurcation theory and numerical simulations.
result: They identify parameter regimes leading to multistability and characterize bifurcation structures.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the design principles of multistable gene circuits.

title: Influence Of Visual Field Offset On Collective Behavior: An Exploration Using The Two-dimensional Vicsek Model
authors: Poorendra Ramlall, Sachit Butail, And Subhradeep Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Poorendra Ramlall, Sachit Butail, and Subhradeep Roy

This study investigates the influence of visual field offset—a restricted field of vision positioned at a fixed angle from an agent's heading direction—on collective behavior using the Vicsek model. This offset shapes an agent's ability to perceive and respond to neighbors, thereby impacting overall…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064409] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how a fixed visual field offset affects collective motion in the Vicsek model, a classical model of self-propelled particles.
motivation: Understanding how sensory limitations like visual field offset influence collective behavior in animal groups.
method: Agent-based simulations of the two-dimensional Vicsek model with a parameter controlling the angular offset of each agent's visual field relative to its heading.
result: The visual field offset significantly alters the onset and nature of collective motion, including changes in order parameters and clustering.
conclusion: Visual field offset is a crucial parameter in collective behavior, and its inclusion in models can better capture realistic animal group dynamics.

title: Flow Of Yield Stress Fluid In A Percolating Network
authors: Nathan Abitbol, Alex Hansen, Alberto Rosso, And Laurent Talon
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Abitbol, Alex Hansen, Alberto Rosso, and Laurent Talon

We study the flow of a Bingham yield stress fluid in a pore network model where the throats have radii drawn from a uniform distribution. We consider the case in which a fraction of the largest radii is blocked. The fluid can flow only through the percolating cluster that exists when the fraction is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065107] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the flow of a Bingham yield stress fluid in a percolating network, focusing on pore-scale physics and rheology.
motivation: Understanding how yield stress fluids flow through porous media is important for applications like enhanced oil recovery and groundwater remediation.
method: The authors use a pore network model with uniformly distributed throat radii, blocking a fraction of the largest radii, and simulate the flow of a Bingham fluid through the percolating cluster.
result: They find that the flow behavior depends on the percolation threshold and the yield stress, with a critical pressure gradient needed for flow.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the interplay between network structure and non-Newtonian fluid rheology, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Performance Enhancement Of Direct-drive Shock-augmented Ignition Inertial Fusion Implosions Through Shock Timing Optimization
authors: M. Khan, K. Churnetski, D. E. M. Barlow, R. Betti, C. Freeman, K. Glize, J. Kunimune, A. Lees, R. Mancini, A. Nutter, R. W. Paddock, S. Regan, C. Stoeckl, W. Theobald, N. Woolsey, And R. H. H. Scott

Shock-augmented ignition (SAI) [R. H. H. Scott et al.,
tldr: This paper optimizes shock timing in inertial confinement fusion implosions to improve performance of shock-augmented ignition.
motivation: Inertial confinement fusion requires high energy gain; shock-augmented ignition offers improved stability and compression, but shock timing must be optimized.
method: The authors use simulations and experiments to adjust shock timing parameters in direct-drive implosions.
result: Optimized shock timing enhances fuel compression and ignition performance.
conclusion: Shock timing optimization is a viable route to improve shock-augmented ignition in inertial fusion.

title: Nanoparticle-mediated Interactions Governing Thermal Gelation Of Protein Dispersions With Tunable Properties
authors: Soumya, Sugam Kumar, Joachim Kohlbrecher, And Vinod K. Aswal
abstract:

Nanoparticle-protein dispersions constitute complex soft materials in which competing attractive and repulsive interactions can strongly influence their phase behavior, including gelation. In this work, we demonstrate a strategy to utilize interaction between anionic silica nanoparticles and anionic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065415] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies gelation in nanoparticle-protein dispersions using small-angle neutron scattering and rheology.
motivation: Understanding how competing interactions govern gelation in soft materials is important for designing tunable properties.
method: The authors use anionic silica nanoparticles and anionic proteins, varying concentration and pH, and characterize structure and dynamics via SANS and rheology.
result: They demonstrate that gelation can be controlled by tuning electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions, leading to tunable mechanical properties.
conclusion: The work provides a strategy for designing protein-based gels with desired properties through nanoparticle-mediated interactions.

title: Enhanced Plasma Production By Ambipolar Electric Fields In Convergent Magnetic Fields
authors: Kazunori Takahashi, Christine Charles, Rod W. Boswell, And Antonella Caldarelli
abstract:
Author(s): Kazunori Takahashi, Christine Charles, Rod W. Boswell, and Antonella Caldarelli

Controlled unidirectional remote plasma production in a radio-frequency (rf) plasma source is demonstrated by placing magnetic nozzle throat several tens of centimeters away from the rf antenna, where a local density peak forms near the throat. The experiment indicates that the dominant electron ene…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023322] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies plasma production in a convergent magnetic field using ambipolar electric fields, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To demonstrate controlled unidirectional remote plasma production in a radio-frequency plasma source with a magnetic nozzle.
method: Experimental setup with a magnetic nozzle throat placed away from the rf antenna, measuring density peaks and electron energy.
result: A local density peak forms near the throat, indicating dominant electron energization by ambipolar electric fields.
conclusion: Ambipolar electric fields in convergent magnetic fields can enhance plasma production, relevant to plasma propulsion and sources.

title: Proof-of-principle Experiment Of A Beam Extraction Over Millions Of Turns Using Stable Resonance Islands And Bent Crystal
authors: D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, And G. Franchetti
abstract:
Author(s): D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. Van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, and G. Franchetti

A recent theoretical investigation indicated that combining particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal may offer a promising option for a low-loss, or even septum-free, slow-extraction technique. This work reports on the successful proof-of-principle experiment conducted at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron, in which stable islands and a bent crystal were employed to split and channel a circulating beam onto an absorber, thereby emulating slow extraction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022055] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a proof-of-principle experiment on beam extraction using resonance islands and a bent crystal at CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron.
motivation: To demonstrate a low-loss, septum-free slow-extraction technique for particle accelerators.
method: Stable resonance islands were used to split the beam, and a bent crystal channeled part of the beam onto an absorber, emulating slow extraction.
result: Successful proof-of-principle demonstration of beam extraction over millions of turns.
conclusion: The technique shows promise for low-loss extraction in high-intensity accelerators.

title: Plasma Flow Generation And Particle Acceleration From Expanding Magnetic Bubbles
authors: Yang Zhang, Brandon K. Russell, Geoffrey Pomraning, Lan Gao, Xiaocan Li, Adam Stanier, William Daughton, Chuanfei Dong, Liang Wang, Peiyun Shi, Kian Orr, And Hantao Ji

Impulsive plasma dynamics in the laboratory are often driven by rising electric currents, yet their quantitative plasma response has not been well established. By means of fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations and laser-driven capacitor-coil experiments, we show that a rising current expels pla…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023317] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.

motivation: To understand impulsive plasma dynamics driven by rising electric currents, which are relevant to astrophysical and laboratory plasmas.
method: Fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations and laser-driven capacitor-coil experiments.
result: A rising current expels plasma and generates fast particles via magnetic bubble expansion.
conclusion: The findings provide quantitative insights into plasma dynamics and particle acceleration in such systems.

title: Leidenfrost Hydrogels: Elastic Surface-wave Instability And Sustained Bouncing
authors: Nathan C. J. Coombs, Peter Lewin-Jones, Mykyta V. Chubynsky, And James E. Sprittles
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan C. J. Coombs, Peter Lewin-Jones, Mykyta V. Chubynsky, and James E. Sprittles

This work investigates the oscillatory dynamics and subsequent sustained bouncing behavior of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a phenomenon that has received little theoretical attention to date. Building on previous approaches toward drop impacts and Leidenfrost drops, a computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics and analyze the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022052] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the oscillatory dynamics and sustained bouncing of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a soft matter fluid dynamics phenomenon.
motivation: Leidenfrost hydrogels exhibit sustained bouncing with little theoretical understanding; the work aims to model the energy injection mechanism.
method: A computational model is developed to capture oscillatory dynamics and analyze the energy injection leading to sustained bouncing.
result: The model reproduces the sustained bouncing behavior and reveals the role of elastic surface-wave instability.
conclusion: The study provides a theoretical framework for understanding sustained bouncing in Leidenfrost hydrogels.

title: Tracking Phase Synchronization Between Flagella In The Time-frequency Domain Resolves Photophobic Response
authors: Lucas Federspiel, Jorge Arrieta, Marco Polin, Françoise Argoul, And Antoine Allard

The unicellular microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (CR) is well known for its biflagellated swimming in response to light stimuli. This work aims to study the resynchronization of CR flagella after a high light intensity stimulus, known as photoshock. The synchronization is estimated thanks to a qu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023294] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flagellar synchronization in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii using time-frequency analysis, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding the resynchronization of flagella after a photophobic response in a unicellular alga.
method: Time-frequency domain analysis to track phase synchronization between two flagella.
result: Quantitative characterization of flagellar resynchronization dynamics following a high-light stimulus.
conclusion: The method effectively resolves the photophobic response and flagellar coordination.

title: Controlled Interference Of Laser-induced Shock Waves In Microdroplet Jetting
authors: R. A. Meijer, G. Lajoinie, B. Liu, S. Witte, And O. O. Versolato

Author(s): R. A. Meijer, G. Lajoinie, B. Liu, S. Witte, and O. O. Versolato

We report the formation of high-velocity microjets driven by the interference of two laser-induced shock waves in a tin microdroplet. A first 0.4-ns laser pulse launches a shock wave into the droplet (diameter [MATH], 50, and [MATH]). Due to the droplet's s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023287] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the formation of high-velocity microjets via controlled interference of laser-induced shock waves in tin microdroplets.
motivation: To understand and control the dynamics of microdroplet jetting for applications such as extreme ultraviolet lithography.
method: Experimental: two laser pulses create interfering shock waves in a tin microdroplet, and high-speed imaging captures the resulting jet formation.
result: The interference pattern can be tuned to control jet velocity and direction, achieving high-speed microjets.
conclusion: Controlled shock wave interference is a viable method for precise microdroplet jetting, with potential in lithography and other fields.

title: Stretching Theory Of Hookean Metashells
authors: Luca Giomi
abstract:

A continuum theory that describes how mechanical metamaterials deform on surfaces takes the form of the Schrödinger equation and provides a different path for materials design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021035] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: A continuum theory for mechanical metamaterials on surfaces is formulated analogously to the Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework for designing mechanical metamaterials that deform on curved surfaces.
method: The author derives a continuum theory that maps the deformation of Hookean metashells to a Schrödinger-like equation.
result: The theory provides a new mathematical description of metashell deformation, enabling novel material design.
conclusion: The work offers a different path for materials design by linking mechanics to quantum-inspired equations.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei

Author(s): Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, and Hai Lei

A force-response model helps understand fatigue behavior and provides a design strategy for fatigue resistant hydrogels and soft materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021031] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is crucial for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical failure at the molecular level and develop a force-response model to connect single-molecule behavior to bulk fatigue.
result: They identify key molecular processes governing fatigue and propose design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work provides a molecular-level understanding of fatigue fracture and offers practical guidelines for creating tougher soft materials.

Cells at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.

tldr: This paper studies cell bulging and extrusion in curved epithelial sheets using a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021019] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
